def cmd_crawl(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    from rag.ingestion.crawler import CrawlConfig, Crawler

    base_urls = [u.strip() for u in args.urls.split(",") if u.strip()]
    raw_dir = _corpus_dir() / "raw"

    config = CrawlConfig(
        base_urls=base_urls,
        output_dir=raw_dir,
        user_agent=args.user_agent,
        delay_seconds=args.delay,
        max_pages=args.max_pages,
        respect_robots=not args.ignore_robots,
        refresh=args.refresh,
        max_depth=args.max_depth,
    )

    if args.ignore_robots:
        print(
            "REFUSING: --ignore-robots is not available.\n"
            "This crawler targets a live institutional website. Ignoring robots.txt\n"
            "is not a technical option we expose.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    print(f"Crawling {', '.join(base_urls)}")
    print(f"  user agent : {config.user_agent}")
    print(f"  delay      : >= {config.delay_seconds}s between requests")
    print(f"  page cap   : {config.max_pages}")
    print(f"  cache      : {raw_dir}")
    print(f"  refresh    : {config.refresh}\n")

    with Crawler(config) as crawler:
        results = crawler.crawl()
        stats = crawler.stats

    print(f"\n{stats.summary()}")
    if stats.error_urls:
        print(f"\nFirst {min(10, len(stats.error_urls))} errors:")
        for line in stats.error_urls[:10]:
            print(f"  {line}")

    html = sum(1 for r in results if "html" in r.content_type)
    pdf = sum(1 for r in results if "pdf" in r.content_type)
    print(f"\nartefacts on disk: {html} HTML, {pdf} PDF")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# dependency preflight
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _preflight() -> int:
    """Report missing optional parsers before they can fail silently.

    Without an HTML extractor, every crawled page yields nothing and the run
    ends with "0 real documents" and no explanation. That is a confusing
    failure to debug, so it is caught here instead.
    """

    def _present(module: str) -> bool:
        try:
            __import__(module)
        except ImportError:
            return False
        return True

    trafilatura = _present("trafilatura")
    beautifulsoup = _present("bs4")
    pymupdf = _present("fitz")

    if not trafilatura and not beautifulsoup:
        print(
            "ERROR: no HTML extractor available. Every crawled page would be\n"
            "       dropped without explanation.\n"
            "       Install with: pip install trafilatura beautifulsoup4 lxml",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1

    if not trafilatura:
        print(
            "WARNING: trafilatura is not installed; falling back to BeautifulSoup.\n"
            "         Boilerplate stripping will be weaker, so site navigation and\n"
            "         footers may end up in the corpus. Install trafilatura for\n"
            "         the intended behaviour.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

    if not pymupdf:
        print(
            "WARNING: PyMuPDF is not installed; PDFs will be skipped and no\n"
            "         page-level provenance will be produced. "
            "Install with: pip install pymupdf",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# parse
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cmd_parse(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if _preflight() != 0:
        return 1

    from rag.ingestion.dedupe import deduplicate, format_report
    from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument
    from rag.ingestion.normalise import normalise
    from rag.ingestion.parsers.html import MIN_USEFUL_CHARS, parse_html
    from rag.ingestion.parsers.markdown import load_demo_corpus
    from rag.ingestion.parsers.pdf import parse_pdf

    corpus = _corpus_dir()
    raw_dir, demo_dir, out_dir = corpus / "raw", corpus / "demo", corpus / "normalised"

    documents: list[ParsedDocument] = []
    failures: list[str] = []
    thin: list[dict[str, str]] = []

    # --- real: crawled HTML and PDFs ---
    for meta_path in sorted(raw_dir.rglob("*.meta.json")):
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            failures.append(f"{meta_path.name}: unreadable metadata")
            continue

        # Use the post-redirect URL when one was recorded. A WordPress
        # "?p=2075" request can 301 to a real slugged page
        # ("/post-with-youtube-video/") -- the pre-redirect url has no
        # meaningful path, so every such request built the same doc_id
        # ("<host>-home") and silently overwrote every other one on disk.
        # ~245 real pages were lost to this before final_url was consulted.
        url = meta.get("final_url") or meta.get("url", "")
        content_type = meta.get("content_type", "")

        # Derive the body filename by APPENDING the extension to the sidecar's
        # stem, never with Path.with_suffix() — which replaces the last suffix.
        # A PDF URL slug already ends in ".pdf", so the cached file is
        # "<slug>.pdf.pdf"; with_suffix() looked for "<slug>.pdf" and silently
        # skipped every PDF in the corpus.
        stem = meta_path.name.removesuffix(".meta.json")
        html_path = meta_path.with_name(f"{stem}.html")
        pdf_path = meta_path.with_name(f"{stem}.pdf")

        # Crawls from this version onward record the path explicitly, so this
        # class of writer/reader disagreement cannot recur.
        recorded = meta.get("local_path")
        if recorded:
            recorded_path = Path(recorded)
            if recorded_path.exists():
                if "pdf" in content_type:
                    pdf_path = recorded_path
                else:
                    html_path = recorded_path

        try:
            if "pdf" in content_type and pdf_path.exists():
                document = parse_pdf(
                    pdf_path,
                    source_url=url,
                    fetched_at=meta.get("fetched_at"),
                    extract_tables=args.tables,
                )
                if document is None:
                    failures.append(
                        f"{pdf_path.name}: too little extractable text "
                        f"(likely a scanned PDF needing OCR)"
                    )
                    continue
            elif html_path.exists():
                document = parse_html(
                    html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"),
                    url=url,
                    local_path=html_path,
                    fetched_at=meta.get("fetched_at"),
                )
                if document is None:
                    # Below MIN_USEFUL_CHARS of body text. Usually right — a
                    # link hub with no prose — but it is a decision about what
                    # the corpus contains, and until it was recorded here it
                    # was the only one in this pipeline that left no trace: not
                    # in this run's output, not in the manifest, not in
                    # suppressed.json. 168 of 993 crawled pages exit this way,
                    # and nothing downstream could say so.
                    thin.append(
                        {"stem": stem, "url": url, "local_path": str(html_path)}
                    )
                    continue
            elif "pdf" in content_type:
                failures.append(
                    f"{stem}: sidecar says PDF but no body file found at {pdf_path.name}"
                )
                continue
            else:
                continue
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad file must not stop the run
            failures.append(f"{stem}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
            continue

        documents.append(document)

    # Same final_url can appear behind more than one raw crawl artifact -- a
    # "?p=1234" query-string request and a slug URL both redirecting to one
    # real page, for instance. Each produces an identical doc_id, and without
    # collapsing them here, normalise() writes each in turn, silently
    # overwriting on disk while still counting every write -- exactly how
    # "written N" can exceed what actually exists in corpus/normalised/.
    seen_ids: dict[str, ParsedDocument] = {}
    duplicate_url_count = 0
    for doc in documents:
        if doc.doc_id in seen_ids:
            duplicate_url_count += 1
            continue
        seen_ids[doc.doc_id] = doc
    if duplicate_url_count:
        print(
            f"same-url duplicates: collapsed {duplicate_url_count} crawl "
            f"artifact(s) resolving to a doc_id already seen"
        )
    documents = list(seen_ids.values())

    real_count = len(documents)

    # --- demo: hand-authored, front matter mandatory ---
    demo_documents, demo_errors = load_demo_corpus(demo_dir)
    documents.extend(demo_documents)
    failures.extend(demo_errors)

    print(
        f"parsed {real_count} real document(s), {len(demo_documents)} demo document(s)"
    )

    # Suppress identical content before anything is written. A hub page whose
    # only substantive block is a shared table is legitimate content once, and
    # noise the other sixty-seven times.
    parsed_total = real_count + len(demo_documents)
    documents, suppressed = deduplicate(documents)
    print(format_report(suppressed, parsed_total))

    _write_discarded_record(corpus, thin)
    if thin:
        print(
            f"discarded {len(thin)} page(s) with under {MIN_USEFUL_CHARS} characters "
            f"of body text (written to corpus/discarded.json)"
        )

    _write_suppression_record(corpus, suppressed)

    result = normalise(documents, out_dir, force=args.force)

    if result.collisions:
        print(
            f"\nABORTED: {len(result.collisions)} document(s) map to a filename "
            f"already used by another.\n"
            f"         Writing would silently destroy one of each pair, so nothing "
            f"was written.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        for stem, first, second in result.collisions[:10]:
            print(
                f"         {stem}\n             {first}\n             {second}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
        return 1

    print(
        f"written {len(result.written)}, unchanged {len(result.unchanged)}, "
        f"pruned {len(result.pruned)}"
    )

    # Reconcile what is on disk against what this run decided to keep. The
    # counts drifting apart is exactly how a suppressed duplicate survives into
    # the corpus unnoticed, so say so loudly rather than leaving it to a later
    # reader of the manifest.
    on_disk = len(list(out_dir.glob("*.json")))
    if on_disk != len(documents):
        print(
            f"\nWARNING: {on_disk} documents on disk but {len(documents)} kept by this run.\n"
            f"         corpus/normalised/ does not match the parse. Re-run with --force.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    else:
        print(
            f"reconciled: parsed {parsed_total}, suppressed {len(suppressed)}, "
            f"kept {len(documents)}, on disk {on_disk}"
        )

    if result.rejected:
        print(f"\nREJECTED {len(result.rejected)} document(s) failing validation:")
        for doc_id, problems in result.rejected[:20]:
            print(f"  {doc_id}")
            for problem in problems:
                print(f"      - {problem}")

    if failures:
        print(f"\n{len(failures)} parse failure(s):")
        for line in failures[:20]:
            print(f"  {line}")
        if len(failures) > 20:
            print(f"  ... and {len(failures) - 20} more")

    return 1 if result.rejected else 0


def _write_discarded_record(corpus: Path, thin: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    """Persist pages dropped for having too little body text.

    Written unconditionally, empty list included, so the absence of discards is
    itself recorded rather than indistinguishable from the file never having
    been produced.
    """
    from rag.ingestion.parsers.html import MIN_USEFUL_CHARS

    path = corpus / "discarded.json"
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "reason": f"under MIN_USEFUL_CHARS ({MIN_USEFUL_CHARS}) of body text",
                "count": len(thin),
                "documents": thin,
            },
            indent=2,
            ensure_ascii=False,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


def _write_suppression_record(corpus: Path, suppressed: list) -> None:
    """Persist suppressions so `manifest` can report them without re-parsing."""
    path = corpus / "suppressed.json"
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps([s.to_dict() for s in suppressed], indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# manifest / stats
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _read_suppression_record(corpus: Path) -> list[dict]:
    path = corpus / "suppressed.json"
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    try:
        return list(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return []


def cmd_manifest(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    from rag.ingestion.manifest import format_stats, load_documents, write_manifest

    corpus = _corpus_dir()
    documents = load_documents(corpus / "normalised")
    if not documents:
        print("No normalised documents found. Run `parse` first.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    suppressed = _read_suppression_record(corpus)
    manifest = write_manifest(documents, corpus / "manifest.json", suppressed)
    print(f"manifest written: {corpus / 'manifest.json'}")
    print()
    print(format_stats(_stats_from(documents, len(suppressed))))

    if not manifest["statistics"]["meets_target"]:
        real_share = manifest["statistics"]["real_share_by_document"]
        print(
            f"\nWARNING: only {real_share:.1%} of the corpus is real data, below the "
            f"80% floor.\n"
            f"         Crawl more real pages, or remove demo documents.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        if args.strict:
            return 1
    return 0


def cmd_stats(_args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    from rag.ingestion.manifest import format_stats, load_documents

    corpus = _corpus_dir()
    documents = load_documents(corpus / "normalised")
    if not documents:
        print("No normalised documents found. Run `parse` first.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(format_stats(_stats_from(documents, len(_read_suppression_record(corpus)))))
    return 0


def _stats_from(documents: list, suppressed: int = 0) -> object:
    from rag.ingestion.manifest import compute_stats

    return compute_stats(documents, suppressed)


def cmd_all(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    for step in (cmd_crawl, cmd_parse, cmd_manifest):
        code = step(args)
        if code not in (0,):
            return code
        print()
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m rag.ingestion",
        description="Corpus ingestion for the PCE knowledge management system.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    def add_crawl_args(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
        p.add_argument(
            "--urls",
            default=_env(
                "CRAWL_BASE_URLS", "https://www.pce.ac.in,https://admissions.pce.ac.in"
            ),
            help="Comma-separated base URLs. Only these hosts are ever fetched.",
        )
        p.add_argument(
            "--delay", type=float, default=float(_env("CRAWL_DELAY_SECONDS", "1.0"))
        )
        p.add_argument(
            "--max-pages", type=int, default=int(_env("CRAWL_MAX_PAGES", "1000"))
        )
        p.add_argument("--max-depth", type=int, default=4)
        p.add_argument(
            "--refresh", action="store_true", help="Re-fetch even if cached."
        )
        p.add_argument("--ignore-robots", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
        p.add_argument(
            "--user-agent",
            default=_env(
                "CRAWL_USER_AGENT",
                "PCE-KMS-AcademicProject/0.1 (B.Tech major project; "
                "contact: bpatil23comp@student.mes.ac.in)",
            ),
        )

    def add_parse_args(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
        p.add_argument(
            "--force", action="store_true", help="Rewrite unchanged documents."
        )
        p.add_argument(
            "--tables", action="store_true", help="Extract PDF tables (slower)."
        )

    def add_manifest_args(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
        p.add_argument(
            "--strict",
            action="store_true",
            help="Exit non-zero if the 80/20 target is missed.",
        )

    crawl = sub.add_parser("crawl", help="Fetch pages and PDFs into corpus/raw/")
    add_crawl_args(crawl)
    crawl.set_defaults(func=cmd_crawl)

    parse_cmd = sub.add_parser("parse", help="Parse raw + demo into corpus/normalised/")
    add_parse_args(parse_cmd)
    parse_cmd.set_defaults(func=cmd_parse)

    manifest = sub.add_parser("manifest", help="Write corpus/manifest.json")
    add_manifest_args(manifest)
    manifest.set_defaults(func=cmd_manifest)

    stats = sub.add_parser("stats", help="Print corpus statistics")
    stats.set_defaults(func=cmd_stats)

    everything = sub.add_parser("all", help="crawl -> parse -> manifest -> stats")
    add_crawl_args(everything)
    add_parse_args(everything)
    add_manifest_args(everything)
    everything.set_defaults(func=cmd_all)

    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    return int(args.func(args))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""A deliberately polite crawler for institutional websites.

Design constraints, in priority order:

1. Be a good guest. Obey robots.txt, identify ourselves with a real contact
   address, rate-limit to roughly one request per second, and never run
   concurrent requests against the same host. Crawling a college's live site
   for a student project is a privilege, not an entitlement.
2. Crawl once. Every response is cached to corpus/raw/ with a metadata
   sidecar. Re-running the pipeline re-reads the cache and does not touch the
   network unless --refresh is passed. Development iterations should cost the
   site nothing.
3. Record provenance for everything. URL, fetch timestamp, HTTP status,
   content type and ETag are stored beside every artefact.

Single-threaded on purpose. At one request per second, concurrency buys
nothing and only risks hammering the host.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import time
from collections import deque
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urldefrag, urljoin, urlparse

import httpx

from rag.ingestion.categorise import is_pdf_url, should_skip

_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"""href\s*=\s*["']([^"'>\s]+)["']""", re.I)
_SITEMAP_LOC_RE = re.compile(r"<loc>\s*([^<\s]+)\s*</loc>", re.I)


@dataclass
class CrawlConfig:
    """Everything the crawler needs. Mirrors the CRAWL_* keys in .env."""

    base_urls: list[str]
    output_dir: Path
    user_agent: str
    delay_seconds: float = 1.0
    max_pages: int = 1000
    timeout_seconds: float = 30.0
    respect_robots: bool = True
    refresh: bool = False
    max_depth: int = 4

    @property
    def allowed_hosts(self) -> set[str]:
        """Only hosts named in base_urls are ever fetched."""
        return {urlparse(u).netloc for u in self.base_urls}


@dataclass
class CrawlResult:
    """One fetched artefact, already written to disk."""

    url: str
    local_path: Path
    content_type: str
    status_code: int
    fetched_at: str
    from_cache: bool
    depth: int


@dataclass
class CrawlStats:
    fetched: int = 0
    from_cache: int = 0
    skipped: int = 0
    disallowed: int = 0
    errors: int = 0
    discovered: int = 0
    error_urls: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def summary(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"fetched={self.fetched} (cache={self.from_cache}) "
            f"skipped={self.skipped} disallowed={self.disallowed} "
            f"errors={self.errors} discovered={self.discovered}"
        )


class Crawler:
    """Breadth-first crawler, seeded from sitemaps where the site offers them."""

    def __init__(self, config: CrawlConfig, robots: object | None = None) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.stats = CrawlStats()
        self._seen: set[str] = set()

        # Imported lazily so tests can construct a Crawler without network.
        if robots is None:
            from rag.ingestion.robots import RobotsPolicy

            robots = RobotsPolicy(
                user_agent=config.user_agent,
                default_delay=config.delay_seconds,
            )
        self.robots = robots

        self._client = httpx.Client(
            headers={"User-Agent": config.user_agent},
            timeout=config.timeout_seconds,
            follow_redirects=True,
        )

    # --- Public API -------------------------------------------------------

    def crawl(self) -> list[CrawlResult]:
        """Crawl every allowed host and return what was fetched."""
        results: list[CrawlResult] = []
        frontier: deque[tuple[str, int]] = deque()

        for base in self.config.base_urls:
            for seed in self._seeds_for(base):
                accepted = self._enqueue(seed)
                if accepted:
                    frontier.append((accepted, 0))

        while frontier and self.stats.fetched < self.config.max_pages:
            url, depth = frontier.popleft()

            result = self._fetch(url, depth)
            if result is None:
                continue
            results.append(result)

            if depth >= self.config.max_depth or is_pdf_url(url):
                continue

            for link in self._links_in(result):
                accepted = self._enqueue(link)
                if accepted:
                    frontier.append((accepted, depth + 1))

        return results

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._client.close()

    def __enter__(self) -> Crawler:
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        self.close()

    # --- Seeding ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _seeds_for(self, base: str) -> list[str]:
        """Prefer the site's own sitemap; fall back to the base URL."""
        seeds: list[str] = [base]
        for sitemap_url in self._sitemap_candidates(base):
            urls = self._read_sitemap(sitemap_url)
            if urls:
                seeds.extend(urls)
                break
        return seeds

    def _sitemap_candidates(self, base: str) -> list[str]:
        declared: list[str] = []
        if self.config.respect_robots and hasattr(self.robots, "sitemaps_for"):
            declared = list(self.robots.sitemaps_for(base))
        conventional = [
            urljoin(base, "/wp-sitemap.xml"),
            urljoin(base, "/sitemap.xml"),
            urljoin(base, "/sitemap_index.xml"),
        ]
        return declared + [c for c in conventional if c not in declared]

    def _read_sitemap(self, sitemap_url: str, depth: int = 0) -> list[str]:
        """Read a sitemap, following one level of sitemap-index nesting."""
        if depth > 1:
            return []
        try:
            response = self._client.get(sitemap_url)
            if response.status_code != 200 or "xml" not in response.headers.get("content-type", ""):
                return []
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            return []

        time.sleep(self.config.delay_seconds)
        locs = _SITEMAP_LOC_RE.findall(response.text)

        if sitemap_url.endswith(("sitemap.xml", "sitemap_index.xml")) and any(
            loc.endswith(".xml") for loc in locs
        ):
            nested: list[str] = []
            for loc in locs:
                if loc.endswith(".xml"):
                    nested.extend(self._read_sitemap(loc, depth + 1))
                else:
                    nested.append(loc)
            return nested
        return [loc for loc in locs if not loc.endswith(".xml")]

    # --- Frontier ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _enqueue(self, url: str) -> str | None:
        """Normalise, deduplicate and filter.

        Returns the NORMALISED url when accepted, and None otherwise. Returning
        it matters: an earlier version normalised only for the dedup set and
        let the caller queue the raw string, so fragments survived into the
        fetch and into the recorded provenance.
        """
        normalised = _normalise_url(url)
        if not normalised or normalised in self._seen:
            return None
        if urlparse(normalised).netloc not in self.config.allowed_hosts:
            return None
        if should_skip(normalised):
            self.stats.skipped += 1
            self._seen.add(normalised)
            return None

        self._seen.add(normalised)
        self.stats.discovered += 1
        return normalised

    # --- Fetching ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _fetch(self, url: str, depth: int) -> CrawlResult | None:
        cached = self._cached(url)
        if cached is not None and not self.config.refresh:
            self.stats.from_cache += 1
            self.stats.fetched += 1
            return cached

        if self.config.respect_robots and not self.robots.can_fetch(url):  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
            self.stats.disallowed += 1
            return None

        try:
            response = self._client.get(url)
        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
            self.stats.errors += 1
            self.stats.error_urls.append(f"{url} :: {type(exc).__name__}")
            return None
        finally:
            delay = (
                self.robots.delay_for(url)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                if self.config.respect_robots and hasattr(self.robots, "delay_for")
                else self.config.delay_seconds
            )
            time.sleep(delay)

        if response.status_code != 200:
            self.stats.errors += 1
            self.stats.error_urls.append(f"{url} :: HTTP {response.status_code}")
            return None

        content_type = response.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";")[0].strip()
        path = self._write(url, response.content, content_type, response)

        self.stats.fetched += 1
        return CrawlResult(
            url=url,
            local_path=path,
            content_type=content_type,
            status_code=response.status_code,
            fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
            from_cache=False,
            depth=depth,
        )

    # --- Cache ------------------------------------------------------------

    def _paths_for(self, url: str) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
        parts = urlparse(url)
        slug = (parts.path or "/").strip("/").replace("/", "__") or "index"
        if parts.query:
            # A STABLE digest, not hash(). Python randomises string hashing per
            # process, so the same URL produced a different cache filename on
            # every run: the cache always missed and the site was re-fetched in
            # full. Politeness depends on this being deterministic.
            digest = hashlib.sha1(parts.query.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
            slug = f"{slug}__q{digest}"
        suffix = ".pdf" if is_pdf_url(url) else ".html"
        base = self.config.output_dir / parts.netloc
        return base / f"{slug}{suffix}", base / f"{slug}.meta.json"

    def _cached(self, url: str) -> CrawlResult | None:
        body_path, meta_path = self._paths_for(url)
        if not (body_path.exists() and meta_path.exists()):
            return None
        try:
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            return None
        return CrawlResult(
            url=url,
            local_path=body_path,
            content_type=meta.get("content_type", ""),
            status_code=meta.get("status_code", 200),
            fetched_at=meta.get("fetched_at", ""),
            from_cache=True,
            depth=meta.get("depth", 0),
        )

    def _write(self, url: str, body: bytes, content_type: str, response: httpx.Response) -> Path:
        body_path, meta_path = self._paths_for(url)
        body_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        body_path.write_bytes(body)
        meta_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "url": url,
                    "final_url": str(response.url),
                    "local_path": str(body_path),
                    "content_type": content_type,
                    "status_code": response.status_code,
                    "fetched_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
                    "etag": response.headers.get("etag"),
                    "last_modified": response.headers.get("last-modified"),
                    "content_length": len(body),
                    "user_agent": self.config.user_agent,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
        )
        return body_path

    # --- Link extraction --------------------------------------------------

    def _links_in(self, result: CrawlResult) -> list[str]:
        if "html" not in result.content_type:
            return []
        try:
            html = result.local_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
        except OSError:
            return []
        return [urljoin(result.url, href) for href in _LINK_RE.findall(html)]


def _normalise_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Strip fragments and trailing slashes so one page is fetched once."""
    url, _ = urldefrag(url.strip())
    if not url.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return ""
    parts = urlparse(url)
    path = parts.path.rstrip("/") or "/"
    rebuilt = f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}{path}"
    return f"{rebuilt}?{parts.query}" if parts.query else rebuilt

"""Suppress documents whose extracted text is identical to another's.

A WordPress site gives many hub pages the same body. On the first real crawl,
68 distinct URLs — /accreditation/, /accreditation/nba/, /iqac/ and 65 others —
produced byte-identical extracted text, because the only substantive block on
each was a shared "Departments" table. Across the corpus that was 97 redundant
documents out of 823, roughly 42,600 wasted words.

Left in, that is not merely untidy. Retrieval would return the same table five
times for a single question, filling the whole context budget with one block
and starving the answer of anything else. Context Precision — one of the three
RAGAS metrics this project reports — measures exactly that, so duplicates would
depress a headline result for a reason that has nothing to do with the
retrieval strategy being evaluated.

Suppression is recorded, never silent. Every suppressed document keeps its URL
in the manifest alongside the document it duplicates, so the corpus can still
answer "did you crawl this page?" with a yes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Suppression:
    """One document dropped as a duplicate of another."""

    doc_id: str
    title: str
    source_url: str | None
    duplicate_of: str
    content_hash: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
        return {
            "doc_id": self.doc_id,
            "title": self.title,
            "source_url": self.source_url,
            "duplicate_of": self.duplicate_of,
            "content_hash": self.content_hash,
        }


def deduplicate(
    documents: list[ParsedDocument],
) -> tuple[list[ParsedDocument], list[Suppression]]:
    """Return (kept, suppressed), preserving the input order of kept documents.

    Documents are grouped by `content_hash`, which is computed over normalised
    text, so two pages differing only in whitespace or casing group together.
    """
    by_hash: dict[str, list[ParsedDocument]] = defaultdict(list)
    for document in documents:
        by_hash[document.content_hash].append(document)

    keep_ids: set[str] = set()
    suppressed: list[Suppression] = []

    for group in by_hash.values():
        if len(group) == 1:
            keep_ids.add(group[0].doc_id)
            continue

        winner = _canonical(group)
        keep_ids.add(winner.doc_id)
        for document in group:
            if document.doc_id == winner.doc_id:
                continue
            suppressed.append(
                Suppression(
                    doc_id=document.doc_id,
                    title=document.title,
                    source_url=document.source_url,
                    duplicate_of=winner.doc_id,
                    content_hash=document.content_hash,
                )
            )

    kept = [d for d in documents if d.doc_id in keep_ids]
    return kept, suppressed


def _canonical(group: list[ParsedDocument]) -> ParsedDocument:
    """Pick which member of a duplicate group to keep.

    Preference order, each a tiebreak for the one above:

    1. Real over demo. A demo document should never collide with a real one,
       but if it ever did, the real document is the one to keep.
    2. Fewest URL path segments. Where /accreditation/ and /accreditation/nba/
       carry the same text, the shallower URL is the more canonical home for
       it.
    3. Shortest URL, then doc_id. Not meaningful in themselves — they make the
       choice deterministic, so two runs over the same corpus keep the same
       document and the manifest does not churn.
    """

    def sort_key(document: ParsedDocument) -> tuple[int, int, int, str]:
        url = document.source_url or document.local_path or ""
        depth = len([p for p in urlparse(url).path.split("/") if p])
        return (int(document.is_demo), depth, len(url), document.doc_id)

    return min(group, key=sort_key)


def format_report(suppressed: list[Suppression], total: int) -> str:
    """A short summary for the CLI."""
    if not suppressed:
        return "deduplication: no duplicate content found"

    groups: dict[str, list[Suppression]] = defaultdict(list)
    for item in suppressed:
        groups[item.duplicate_of].append(item)

    share = len(suppressed) / total if total else 0.0
    lines = [
        f"deduplication: suppressed {len(suppressed)} of {total} documents "
        f"({share:.1%}) across {len(groups)} duplicate group(s)",
    ]

    worst = sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: len(kv[1]), reverse=True)[:5]
    for kept_id, items in worst:
        lines.append(f"    {len(items) + 1} copies -> kept {kept_id}")
        for item in items[:2]:
            lines.append(f"        dropped {item.source_url or item.doc_id}")
        if len(items) > 2:
            lines.append(f"        ... and {len(items) - 2} more")

    return "\n".join(lines)

"""The corpus manifest: one file that answers "what is in the corpus, and
where did each piece come from?"

corpus/manifest.json is the contract between Phase 1 and everything after it.
Phase 2 loads it into PostgreSQL; the admin console reads its statistics; the
report quotes its real-versus-demo ratio. Because it records provenance for
every document, any claim the finished system makes can be walked back to a
URL and a fetch timestamp.

The ratio is reported two ways. By **document count**, because that is the
target stated in the plan. By **word count**, because ten one-paragraph notices
and ten forty-page reports are not the same contribution to a corpus, and a
count-only figure can be quietly misleading.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument

MANIFEST_VERSION = 1

MIN_REAL_SHARE = 0.80
"""The corpus must be at least this proportion real institutional data.

This is a FLOOR, not a band. The project brief asks for "~80% real, ~20%
clearly labelled demo", and the intent of that is a guarantee about how much of
what the system knows is genuine. A corpus that is 97% real over-delivers on
that guarantee; it is not a defect, and an earlier two-sided check that
reported it as one was wrong.

Demo share is still reported, because it answers a different and useful
question: is there enough internal-document coverage to evaluate that retrieval
path? That question is answered by counting golden-set questions, not by a
percentage, so it is reported for information rather than enforced.
"""


@dataclass
class CorpusStats:
    total_documents: int
    real_documents: int
    demo_documents: int
    total_words: int
    real_words: int
    demo_words: int
    by_category: dict[str, int]
    by_source_type: dict[str, int]
    by_department: dict[str, int]
    documents_with_page_provenance: int
    total_sections: int
    duplicates_suppressed: int = 0

    @property
    def demo_share_by_document(self) -> float:
        return (
            self.demo_documents / self.total_documents if self.total_documents else 0.0
        )

    @property
    def demo_share_by_word(self) -> float:
        return self.demo_words / self.total_words if self.total_words else 0.0

    @property
    def real_share_by_document(self) -> float:
        return (
            self.real_documents / self.total_documents if self.total_documents else 0.0
        )

    @property
    def meets_target(self) -> bool:
        """True when at least MIN_REAL_SHARE of the corpus is real data."""
        return self.real_share_by_document >= MIN_REAL_SHARE

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "total_documents": self.total_documents,
            "real_documents": self.real_documents,
            "demo_documents": self.demo_documents,
            "real_share_by_document": round(self.real_share_by_document, 4),
            "demo_share_by_document": round(self.demo_share_by_document, 4),
            "demo_share_by_word": round(self.demo_share_by_word, 4),
            "min_real_share": MIN_REAL_SHARE,
            "meets_target": self.meets_target,
            "total_words": self.total_words,
            "real_words": self.real_words,
            "demo_words": self.demo_words,
            "total_sections": self.total_sections,
            "duplicates_suppressed": self.duplicates_suppressed,
            "documents_with_page_provenance": self.documents_with_page_provenance,
            "by_category": self.by_category,
            "by_source_type": self.by_source_type,
            "by_department": self.by_department,
        }


def compute_stats(
    documents: list[ParsedDocument], duplicates_suppressed: int = 0
) -> CorpusStats:
    real = [d for d in documents if not d.is_demo]
    demo = [d for d in documents if d.is_demo]

    return CorpusStats(
        total_documents=len(documents),
        real_documents=len(real),
        demo_documents=len(demo),
        total_words=sum(d.word_count for d in documents),
        real_words=sum(d.word_count for d in real),
        demo_words=sum(d.word_count for d in demo),
        by_category=dict(Counter(d.category.value for d in documents).most_common()),
        by_source_type=dict(
            Counter(d.source_type.value for d in documents).most_common()
        ),
        by_department=dict(
            Counter(d.department for d in documents if d.department).most_common()
        ),
        documents_with_page_provenance=sum(
            1 for d in documents if any(s.start_page is not None for s in d.sections)
        ),
        total_sections=sum(len(d.sections) for d in documents),
        duplicates_suppressed=duplicates_suppressed,
    )


def build_manifest(
    documents: list[ParsedDocument],
    suppressed: list[Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The manifest: statistics, a provenance row per document, and a
    record of every document suppressed as a duplicate.

    Suppressed documents are listed rather than forgotten, so the corpus
    can still answer "was this page crawled?" with a yes and a pointer to
    the document that carries its content.
    """
    suppressed = suppressed or []
    return {
        "manifest_version": MANIFEST_VERSION,
        "generated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
        "statistics": compute_stats(documents, len(suppressed)).to_dict(),
        "suppressed_duplicates": [
            item.to_dict() if hasattr(item, "to_dict") else item for item in suppressed
        ],
        "documents": [
            {
                "doc_id": d.doc_id,
                # The filename its .md/.json were written under. Carried
                # explicitly because doc_id -> filename is a lossy
                # transformation (slugify truncates at 80 characters), and a
                # consumer that re-derives it will get it wrong for any long
                # id. The seed loader did exactly that and silently skipped 27
                # documents.
                "file_stem": d.file_stem,
                "title": d.title,
                "category": d.category.value,
                "source_type": d.source_type.value,
                "source_url": d.source_url,
                "local_path": d.local_path,
                "fetched_at": d.fetched_at,
                "content_hash": d.content_hash,
                "department": d.department,
                "published_date": d.published_date,
                "page_count": d.page_count,
                "word_count": d.word_count,
                "section_count": len(d.sections),
                "has_page_provenance": any(
                    s.start_page is not None for s in d.sections
                ),
                "is_demo": d.is_demo,
                "demo_reason": d.demo_reason,
            }
            for d in sorted(
                documents, key=lambda x: (x.is_demo, x.category.value, x.doc_id)
            )
        ],
    }


def write_manifest(
    documents: list[ParsedDocument],
    path: Path,
    suppressed: list[Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    manifest = build_manifest(documents, suppressed)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    return manifest


def load_documents(normalised_dir: Path) -> list[ParsedDocument]:
    """Rebuild ParsedDocuments from corpus/normalised/*.json."""
    from rag.ingestion.models import DocumentCategory, Section, SourceType

    documents: list[ParsedDocument] = []
    for path in sorted(normalised_dir.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            continue
        sections = [Section(**s) for s in raw.pop("sections", [])]
        raw["source_type"] = SourceType(raw["source_type"])
        raw["category"] = DocumentCategory(raw["category"])
        documents.append(ParsedDocument(sections=sections, **raw))
    return documents


def format_stats(stats: CorpusStats) -> str:
    """A readable summary for the CLI and for pasting into the report."""
    lines = [
        "Corpus statistics",
        "=================",
        f"  documents          {stats.total_documents}",
        f"    real             {stats.real_documents}",
        f"    demo             {stats.demo_documents}",
        f"  sections           {stats.total_sections}",
        f"  duplicates dropped {stats.duplicates_suppressed}",
        f"  words              {stats.total_words:,}",
        f"  page provenance    {stats.documents_with_page_provenance} documents "
        f"(PDFs carry page numbers; HTML has no pages)",
        "",
        "Real vs demo",
        "------------",
        f"  real               {stats.real_share_by_document:.1%} of documents "
        f"(floor: {MIN_REAL_SHARE:.0%})",
        f"  demo               {stats.demo_share_by_document:.1%} of documents, "
        f"{stats.demo_share_by_word:.1%} of words",
        f"  floor met          {'YES' if stats.meets_target else 'NO'}",
    ]

    if stats.by_category:
        lines += ["", "By category", "-----------"]
        width = max(len(k) for k in stats.by_category)
        lines += [f"  {k:<{width}}  {v}" for k, v in stats.by_category.items()]

    if stats.by_department:
        lines += ["", "By department", "-------------"]
        width = max(len(k) for k in stats.by_department)
        lines += [f"  {k:<{width}}  {v}" for k, v in stats.by_department.items()]

    if stats.by_source_type:
        lines += ["", "By source type", "--------------"]
        width = max(len(k) for k in stats.by_source_type)
        lines += [f"  {k:<{width}}  {v}" for k, v in stats.by_source_type.items()]

    return "\n".join(lines)

"""The data model every parser produces and every consumer reads.

One rule governs this module: a document is never separated from its
provenance. `source_url`, `fetched_at`, `content_hash` and `is_demo` travel
with the document into normalisation, into the database, into retrieval, and
finally into the citation a user sees. Research gap 4 (inadequate grounding and
explainability) is closed here, not in the prompt.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Any


class SourceType(StrEnum):
    """Where a document's bytes came from."""

    WEB_HTML = "web_html"
    WEB_PDF = "web_pdf"
    LOCAL_MARKDOWN = "local_markdown"


class DocumentCategory(StrEnum):
    """What a document is about.

    Drives metadata filtering at retrieval time: a question about intake should
    search PROGRAMME and ADMISSION, not twenty years of event announcements.
    """

    # --- Real, public categories ---
    INSTITUTE_PROFILE = "institute_profile"
    ACCREDITATION = "accreditation"
    PROGRAMME = "programme"
    CURRICULUM = "curriculum"
    DEPARTMENT = "department"
    FACULTY = "faculty"
    RESEARCH = "research"
    LIBRARY = "library"
    STUDENT_LIFE = "student_life"
    PLACEMENT = "placement"
    ADMISSION = "admission"
    ANNOUNCEMENT = "announcement"
    EVENT = "event"
    REPORT = "report"
    GOVERNANCE = "governance"
    CONTACT = "contact"
    ALUMNI = "alumni"

    # --- Demo-only categories: internal material no institution publishes ---
    INTERNAL_WIKI = "internal_wiki"
    SOP = "sop"
    CIRCULAR = "circular"
    LAB_MANUAL = "lab_manual"
    HELPDESK = "helpdesk"
    TIMETABLE = "timetable"

    OTHER = "other"

    @property
    def is_internal_only(self) -> bool:
        """True for categories that can only ever be demo data.

        If a document in one of these categories is ever marked is_demo=False,
        something has gone wrong: this material is not public anywhere.
        """
        return self in {
            DocumentCategory.INTERNAL_WIKI,
            DocumentCategory.SOP,
            DocumentCategory.CIRCULAR,
            DocumentCategory.LAB_MANUAL,
            DocumentCategory.HELPDESK,
            DocumentCategory.TIMETABLE,
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Section:
    """One node of a document's heading hierarchy.

    `section_path` is the breadcrumb a citation shows the user, e.g.
    "Academics > B.Tech > Computer Engineering > Curriculum". `start_page` is
    set for PDFs and is what makes page-level provenance possible; it is None
    for HTML, which has no pages.
    """

    heading: str
    level: int
    content: str
    order_index: int
    section_path: str = ""
    parent_index: int | None = None
    start_page: int | None = None
    end_page: int | None = None

    @property
    def char_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.content)

    @property
    def is_substantive(self) -> bool:
        """False for headings with no body — navigation stubs, mostly."""
        return self.char_count >= 40


@dataclass(slots=True)
class ParsedDocument:
    """A document after parsing, before chunking.

    Chunking (Phase 4) consumes `sections`; the naive baseline C0 (Phase 3)
    consumes `text` and ignores the hierarchy entirely. Holding both is what
    lets the two configurations run over identical source material.
    """

    doc_id: str
    title: str
    source_type: SourceType
    category: DocumentCategory
    text: str
    sections: list[Section] = field(default_factory=list)

    # --- Provenance: never optional in spirit, even where typed optional ---
    source_url: str | None = None
    local_path: str | None = None
    fetched_at: str = ""
    content_hash: str = ""

    # --- Descriptive metadata ---
    department: str | None = None
    published_date: str | None = None
    author: str | None = None
    page_count: int | None = None
    language: str = "en"

    # --- Real vs demo ---
    is_demo: bool = False
    demo_reason: str | None = None

    extra: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.fetched_at:
            self.fetched_at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
        if not self.content_hash:
            self.content_hash = compute_content_hash(self.text)

    # --- Invariants -------------------------------------------------------
    def validate(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return a list of problems. Empty list means the document is sound.

        Called by the normaliser before anything is written to disk, so a
        malformed document fails at ingestion rather than surfacing later as a
        citation that points nowhere.
        """
        problems: list[str] = []

        if not self.doc_id:
            problems.append("doc_id is empty")
        if not self.title.strip():
            problems.append("title is empty")
        if not self.text.strip():
            problems.append("text is empty")
        if not self.fetched_at:
            problems.append("fetched_at is empty")
        if not self.content_hash:
            problems.append("content_hash is empty")

        if self.source_url is None and self.local_path is None:
            problems.append("no provenance: both source_url and local_path are None")

        if self.is_demo and not self.demo_reason:
            problems.append("is_demo is True but demo_reason is missing")
        if not self.is_demo and self.category.is_internal_only:
            problems.append(
                f"category '{self.category.value}' is internal-only and cannot be real data; "
                "either mark is_demo=True or re-categorise"
            )

        if (
            self.source_type is SourceType.WEB_PDF
            and self.sections
            and not any(s.start_page is not None for s in self.sections)
        ):
            problems.append("PDF document has no page numbers on any section")

        return problems

    @property
    def file_stem(self) -> str:
        """A filesystem-safe name derived from doc_id.

        doc_id is deliberately allowed to be a real-world identifier such as
        "DEMO/EXAM/2026/03" — that is what a circular number actually looks
        like, and flattening it would make the corpus less faithful. But those
        slashes are path separators, so anything writing a file uses this
        instead. The identifier stays intact in the metadata and the manifest.
        """
        return slugify(self.doc_id.replace("/", "-"))

    @property
    def word_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.text.split())

    @property
    def substantive_sections(self) -> list[Section]:
        return [s for s in self.sections if s.is_substantive]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        d = asdict(self)
        d["source_type"] = self.source_type.value
        d["category"] = self.category.value
        return d


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_SLUG_STRIP = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def compute_content_hash(text: str) -> str:
    """Hash the *normalised text*, not the raw bytes.

    A WordPress page whose sidebar advert changed produces different bytes but
    identical extracted text. Hashing the text means a re-crawl only re-ingests
    documents whose content actually changed, which keeps repeat crawls cheap
    and keeps the site's load down.
    """
    normalised = _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", text).strip().lower()
    return hashlib.sha256(normalised.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def slugify(value: str, max_length: int = 80) -> str:
    """Lowercase, hyphenated, filesystem-safe."""
    slug = _SLUG_STRIP.sub("-", value.lower()).strip("-")
    if len(slug) > max_length:
        slug = slug[:max_length].rstrip("-")
    return slug or "untitled"

"""Write parsed documents to corpus/normalised/ in a stable, reviewable form.

Two files per document:

    <doc_id>.md    front matter + body, with section markers. Human-readable,
                   diffable, and what a supervisor can open to check the
                   corpus by eye.
    <doc_id>.json  the full structured record, including every section with
                   its heading path and page range. This is what Phase 2 loads
                   into PostgreSQL and Phase 4 chunks.

Validation runs before anything is written. A document that fails its
invariants is reported and skipped rather than written, so the corpus on disk
is always sound.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument


@dataclass
class NormaliseResult:
    written: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rejected: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = field(default_factory=list)
    unchanged: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    pruned: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    collisions: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    """(file_stem, first doc_id, colliding doc_id) — nothing is written when
    this is non-empty, because writing would destroy one of them."""

    @property
    def total(self) -> int:
        return len(self.written) + len(self.unchanged)


def normalise(
    documents: list[ParsedDocument],
    output_dir: Path,
    *,
    force: bool = False,
    prune: bool = True,
) -> NormaliseResult:
    """Validate and write documents, then remove anything else.

    Pruning is not housekeeping — it is what makes the directory *mean*
    something. Without it, normalise only ever added: a document dropped by
    deduplication, or one that stopped being crawled, kept its file forever.
    The first deduplicating run suppressed 214 documents and 200 of them
    survived on disk, so `load_documents` read them straight back and the
    manifest reported a corpus that still contained every duplicate. The
    deduplication was, in effect, a no-op.

    The directory is a generated artefact and is gitignored, so it is safe to
    treat as derived state: after this call it contains exactly the documents
    passed in, and nothing else.
    """
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result = NormaliseResult()

    # doc_id -> file_stem is lossy: slugify truncates at 80 characters, so two
    # long ids sharing a prefix would map to one file and the second would
    # overwrite the first. That loss would be invisible — the manifest would
    # list both documents while only one existed on disk. Detect it and refuse
    # rather than discover it later as a document that cannot be found.
    seen_stems: dict[str, str] = {}
    for document in documents:
        clash = seen_stems.get(document.file_stem)
        if clash is not None and clash != document.doc_id:
            result.collisions.append((document.file_stem, clash, document.doc_id))
        seen_stems.setdefault(document.file_stem, document.doc_id)

    if result.collisions:
        return result

    for document in documents:
        problems = document.validate()
        if problems:
            result.rejected.append((document.doc_id or "<no id>", problems))
            continue

        json_path = output_dir / f"{document.file_stem}.json"
        if not force and _hash_unchanged(json_path, document.content_hash):
            result.unchanged.append(document.doc_id)
            continue

        (output_dir / f"{document.file_stem}.md").write_text(
            _to_markdown(document), encoding="utf-8"
        )
        json_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(document.to_dict(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        result.written.append(document.doc_id)

    if prune and documents:
        # `documents` is empty when a parse failed outright. Pruning then would
        # delete the whole corpus on the strength of a broken run, so don't.
        result.pruned = _prune(output_dir, documents)

    return result


def _prune(output_dir: Path, documents: list[ParsedDocument]) -> list[str]:
    """Delete outputs for documents no longer in the corpus."""
    expected = {d.file_stem for d in documents}
    removed: list[str] = []
    for path in sorted(output_dir.iterdir()):
        if path.suffix not in (".json", ".md") or path.stem in expected:
            continue
        try:
            path.unlink()
            removed.append(path.name)
        except OSError:
            continue
    return removed


def _hash_unchanged(json_path: Path, content_hash: str) -> bool:
    """Skip rewriting a document whose extracted text has not changed."""
    if not json_path.exists():
        return False
    try:
        existing = json.loads(json_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return False
    return bool(existing.get("content_hash") == content_hash)


def _to_markdown(document: ParsedDocument) -> str:
    """Front matter plus body, with an explicit marker per section.

    The markers are not decoration: they let a reader confirm by eye that the
    structure-aware chunker split where the document actually changes topic.
    """
    lines = [
        "---",
        f"doc_id: {document.doc_id}",
        f"title: {json.dumps(document.title, ensure_ascii=False)}",
        f"category: {document.category.value}",
        f"source_type: {document.source_type.value}",
        f"source_url: {document.source_url or ''}",
        f"local_path: {document.local_path or ''}",
        f"fetched_at: {document.fetched_at}",
        f"content_hash: {document.content_hash}",
        f"department: {document.department or ''}",
        f"published_date: {document.published_date or ''}",
        f"page_count: {document.page_count if document.page_count is not None else ''}",
        f"word_count: {document.word_count}",
        f"section_count: {len(document.sections)}",
        f"is_demo: {str(document.is_demo).lower()}",
    ]
    if document.is_demo:
        lines.append(
            f"demo_reason: {json.dumps(document.demo_reason, ensure_ascii=False)}"
        )
    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")

    if document.is_demo:
        lines.append("> **DEMO DATA** — this document is synthetic. It does not")
        lines.append("> describe any real institutional fact, person or figure.")
        lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"# {document.title}")
    lines.append("")

    if not document.sections:
        lines.append(document.text)
        return "\n".join(lines)

    for section in document.sections:
        pages = ""
        if section.start_page is not None:
            pages = (
                f", page {section.start_page}"
                if section.start_page == section.end_page
                else f", pages {section.start_page}-{section.end_page}"
            )
        lines.append(f"<!-- section: {section.section_path}{pages} -->")
        lines.append(f"{'#' * min(section.level + 1, 6)} {section.heading}")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(section.content)
        lines.append("")

    return "\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n"
