"""Demo corpus loader — the gatekeeper for synthetic data.

Every file under corpus/demo/ must carry YAML front matter declaring what it
is and why it is synthetic. A file without it is REJECTED, not defaulted.

That strictness is the whole point. `is_demo` propagates from here into the
database, into every chunk, and into every citation the user sees. If a
synthetic document could slip through unlabelled, the 80/20 real-versus-demo
claim would be decoration rather than a guarantee — and an examiner would be
right to distrust every number in Chapter 4.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from rag.ingestion.models import DocumentCategory, ParsedDocument, SourceType, slugify
from rag.ingestion.parsers.sections import sections_from_markdown

REQUIRED_KEYS = ("title", "doc_id", "is_demo", "demo_reason", "category")

_FENCE = "---"


class DemoFrontMatterError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a demo document is missing or misusing its front matter."""


def parse_demo_markdown(path: Path) -> ParsedDocument:
    """Load one demo document. Raises DemoFrontMatterError if non-compliant."""
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    meta, body = _split_front_matter(raw, path)

    missing = [key for key in REQUIRED_KEYS if key not in meta]
    if missing:
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(
            f"{path.name}: front matter is missing required key(s): {', '.join(missing)}. "
            f"Required: {', '.join(REQUIRED_KEYS)}."
        )

    if meta["is_demo"] is not True:
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(
            f"{path.name}: is_demo must be literally true. Everything under "
            f"corpus/demo/ is synthetic by definition; a file that is not demo "
            f"data does not belong in this folder."
        )

    reason = str(meta.get("demo_reason", "")).strip()
    if len(reason) < 20:
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(
            f"{path.name}: demo_reason must explain why this document is synthetic "
            f"(at least 20 characters). Got: {reason!r}"
        )

    try:
        category = DocumentCategory(str(meta["category"]))
    except ValueError as exc:
        valid = ", ".join(c.value for c in DocumentCategory)
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(
            f"{path.name}: unknown category {meta['category']!r}. Valid: {valid}"
        ) from exc

    if not body.strip():
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(f"{path.name}: document body is empty.")

    title = str(meta["title"]).strip()
    return ParsedDocument(
        doc_id=str(meta["doc_id"]).strip() or f"demo-{slugify(path.stem)}",
        title=title,
        source_type=SourceType.LOCAL_MARKDOWN,
        category=category,
        text=body.strip(),
        sections=sections_from_markdown(body, root_title=title),
        source_url=None,
        local_path=str(path),
        fetched_at=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
        department=_optional_str(meta.get("department")),
        published_date=_optional_str(meta.get("created")),
        author=_optional_str(meta.get("author")),
        is_demo=True,
        demo_reason=reason,
        extra={"demo_identifier": _optional_str(meta.get("doc_id"))},
    )


def load_demo_corpus(demo_dir: Path) -> tuple[list[ParsedDocument], list[str]]:
    """Load every demo document. Returns (documents, errors).

    Errors are collected rather than raised so one malformed file reports
    clearly instead of aborting the whole ingest.
    """
    documents: list[ParsedDocument] = []
    errors: list[str] = []

    for path in sorted(demo_dir.rglob("*.md")):
        if path.name.upper().startswith("README"):
            continue
        try:
            documents.append(parse_demo_markdown(path))
        except DemoFrontMatterError as exc:
            errors.append(str(exc))
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - report, do not abort
            errors.append(f"{path.name}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    return documents, errors


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _split_front_matter(raw: str, path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:
    stripped = raw.lstrip("﻿").lstrip()
    if not stripped.startswith(_FENCE):
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(
            f"{path.name}: no YAML front matter. Every file in corpus/demo/ must "
            f"begin with a '---' block declaring at least: {', '.join(REQUIRED_KEYS)}. "
            f"See corpus/demo/README.md."
        )

    parts = stripped.split(_FENCE, 2)
    if len(parts) < 3:
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(f"{path.name}: front matter block is not closed with '---'.")

    try:
        import yaml
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - dependency guard
        raise RuntimeError("PyYAML is required: pip install pyyaml") from exc

    try:
        meta = yaml.safe_load(parts[1]) or {}
    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(f"{path.name}: front matter is not valid YAML: {exc}") from exc

    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
        raise DemoFrontMatterError(f"{path.name}: front matter must be a YAML mapping.")

    return meta, parts[2]


def _optional_str(value: object) -> str | None:
    if value is None:
        return None
    text = str(value).strip()
    return text or None


__all__ = ["DemoFrontMatterError", "REQUIRED_KEYS", "load_demo_corpus", "parse_demo_markdown"]

"""PDF -> ParsedDocument, with page numbers on every section.

Page-level provenance is a hard requirement of this project: a citation must
be able to say "Annual Report 2023-24, section 4.2, page 37". Everything here
serves that.

Heading detection uses three strategies in descending order of reliability:

1. The PDF's embedded table of contents. Institutional PDFs produced from Word
   (annual reports, NAAC submissions, IQAC reports) almost always carry one,
   and it is authoritative — it is the author's own structure.
2. Font-size analysis. Text noticeably larger than the document's body size is
   treated as a heading, with levels assigned by size rank.
3. One section per page. Always correct, never useful, but it guarantees page
   provenance even for a scanned or badly generated file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import statistics
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

from rag.ingestion.categorise import categorise, infer_department
from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument, Section, SourceType, slugify

MIN_USEFUL_CHARS = 400
HEADING_SIZE_RATIO = 1.15
"""A span must be this much larger than body text to count as a heading."""

import re

_PAGE_NUMBER_LIKE = re.compile(r"^(page\s*)?\d{1,4}$", re.IGNORECASE)


def _looks_like_page_number(text: str) -> bool:
    """True for printed page-number labels ("Page 36", "36", "- 36 -").

    Font-size analysis alone cannot tell a real heading from a page number
    printed in a large running header or footer -- both are short and
    large. Rejecting anything that is just digits (with an optional "Page"
    prefix) keeps a footer artifact from becoming a section heading whose
    number then disagrees with the section's real `start_page`.
    """
    return bool(_PAGE_NUMBER_LIKE.match(text.strip().strip("-").strip()))


def parse_pdf(
    path: Path,
    *,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    fetched_at: str | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    extract_tables: bool = False,
    min_chars: int = MIN_USEFUL_CHARS,
) -> ParsedDocument | None:
    """Parse a PDF. Returns None if too little text could be extracted.

    A None return on a large file usually means the PDF is scanned images, in
    which case OCR is required — reported by the CLI rather than silently
    dropped, because a missing annual report is a corpus gap worth knowing
    about.
    """
    try:
        import fitz  # PyMuPDF
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - dependency guard
        raise RuntimeError("PyMuPDF is required to parse PDFs: pip install pymupdf") from exc

    with fitz.open(path) as document:
        pages = [page.get_text("text") for page in document]
        toc = document.get_toc() or []
        metadata = document.metadata or {}
        page_count = document.page_count
        spans = _collect_spans(document) if not toc else []

    full_text = "\n\n".join(pages).strip()
    if len(full_text) < min_chars:
        return None

    resolved_title = (
        title
        or (metadata.get("title") or "").strip()
        or path.stem.replace("-", " ").replace("_", " ").title()
    )

    if toc:
        sections = _sections_from_toc(toc, pages, resolved_title)
    elif spans:
        sections = _sections_from_spans(spans, pages, resolved_title)
    else:
        sections = _sections_per_page(pages, resolved_title)

    if extract_tables:
        _append_tables(path, sections)

    reference = source_url or str(path)
    return ParsedDocument(
        doc_id=_doc_id_for(path, source_url),
        title=resolved_title,
        source_type=SourceType.WEB_PDF,
        category=categorise(reference),
        text=full_text,
        sections=sections,
        source_url=source_url,
        local_path=str(path),
        fetched_at=fetched_at or datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
        department=infer_department(reference, full_text),
        author=(metadata.get("author") or "").strip() or None,
        published_date=_normalise_pdf_date(metadata.get("creationDate")),
        page_count=page_count,
        is_demo=False,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strategy 1: embedded table of contents
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _sections_from_toc(toc: list[list], pages: list[str], root_title: str) -> list[Section]:
    """Build sections from [level, title, page] entries.

    Each entry's content runs from its own start page to the page before the
    next entry, which is why start_page and end_page are both meaningful.
    """
    sections: list[Section] = []
    open_stack: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    for i, entry in enumerate(toc):
        level, heading, page_no = int(entry[0]), str(entry[1]).strip(), int(entry[2])
        start = max(1, page_no)
        end = int(toc[i + 1][2]) - 1 if i + 1 < len(toc) else len(pages)
        end = max(start, min(end, len(pages)))

        content = "\n\n".join(pages[start - 1 : end]).strip()

        while open_stack and open_stack[-1][0] >= level:
            open_stack.pop()
        parent_index = open_stack[-1][1] if open_stack else None
        ancestors = [sections[idx].heading for _, idx in open_stack]
        section_path = " > ".join([root_title, *ancestors, heading])

        index = len(sections)
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=heading,
                level=level,
                content=content,
                order_index=index,
                section_path=section_path,
                parent_index=parent_index,
                start_page=start,
                end_page=end,
            )
        )
        open_stack.append((level, index))

    return sections or _sections_per_page(pages, root_title)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strategy 2: font-size analysis
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _collect_spans(document: object) -> list[tuple[int, float, str]]:
    """Return (page_number, font_size, text) for every non-empty span."""
    spans: list[tuple[int, float, str]] = []
    for page_index, page in enumerate(document, start=1):  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        try:
            data = page.get_text("dict")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for block in data.get("blocks", []):
            for line in block.get("lines", []):
                text = "".join(s.get("text", "") for s in line.get("spans", [])).strip()
                if not text:
                    continue
                sizes = [
                    s.get("size", 0.0) for s in line.get("spans", []) if s.get("text", "").strip()
                ]
                if sizes:
                    spans.append((page_index, max(sizes), text))
    return spans


def _sections_from_spans(
    spans: list[tuple[int, float, str]], pages: list[str], root_title: str
) -> list[Section]:
    """Treat spans meaningfully larger than body text as headings."""
    sizes = [size for _, size, _ in spans]
    body_size = statistics.median(sizes) if sizes else 0.0
    threshold = body_size * HEADING_SIZE_RATIO

    heading_sizes = sorted({round(s, 1) for s in sizes if s >= threshold}, reverse=True)
    level_of = {size: min(i + 1, 6) for i, size in enumerate(heading_sizes[:6])}

    sections: list[Section] = []
    current_heading = root_title
    current_level = 1
    current_page = 1
    buffer: list[str] = []

    def flush(end_page: int) -> None:
        content = "\n".join(buffer).strip()
        if not content:
            return
        index = len(sections)
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=current_heading,
                level=current_level,
                content=content,
                order_index=index,
                section_path=f"{root_title} > {current_heading}"
                if current_heading != root_title
                else root_title,
                start_page=current_page,
                end_page=end_page,
            )
        )

    for page_no, size, text in spans:
        rounded = round(size, 1)
        is_heading = (
            rounded in level_of
            and 3 <= len(text) <= 120
            and not _looks_like_page_number(text)
        )
        if is_heading:
            flush(page_no)
            buffer = []
            current_heading = text
            current_level = level_of[rounded]
            current_page = page_no
        else:
            buffer.append(text)

    flush(len(pages))
    return sections or _sections_per_page(pages, root_title)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Strategy 3: one section per page
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _sections_per_page(pages: list[str], root_title: str) -> list[Section]:
    sections: list[Section] = []
    for page_index, text in enumerate(pages, start=1):
        content = text.strip()
        if not content:
            continue
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=f"Page {page_index}",
                level=1,
                content=content,
                order_index=len(sections),
                section_path=f"{root_title} > Page {page_index}",
                start_page=page_index,
                end_page=page_index,
            )
        )
    return sections


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tables
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _append_tables(path: Path, sections: list[Section]) -> None:
    """Append markdown tables to whichever section covers their page.

    Institutional PDFs carry a lot of meaning in tables — intake numbers,
    placement statistics, committee membership. Flattened to prose by plain
    text extraction they become unreadable; as markdown the LLM can read them.
    """
    try:
        import pdfplumber
    except ImportError:
        return

    try:
        with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
            for page_index, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
                for table in page.extract_tables() or []:
                    markdown = _table_to_markdown(table)
                    if not markdown:
                        continue
                    target = _section_covering(sections, page_index)
                    if target is not None:
                        target.content = f"{target.content}\n\n{markdown}".strip()
    except Exception:
        # Table extraction is a bonus; never let it fail an ingest.
        return


def _section_covering(sections: list[Section], page_no: int) -> Section | None:
    for section in sections:
        if (
            section.start_page is not None
            and section.end_page is not None
            and section.start_page <= page_no <= section.end_page
        ):
            return section
    return sections[-1] if sections else None


def _table_to_markdown(table: list[list[str | None]]) -> str:
    rows = [[(cell or "").replace("\n", " ").strip() for cell in row] for row in table if row]
    rows = [r for r in rows if any(r)]
    if len(rows) < 2:
        return ""
    width = max(len(r) for r in rows)
    rows = [r + [""] * (width - len(r)) for r in rows]
    header, *body = rows
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "---|" * width]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in body]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _doc_id_for(path: Path, source_url: str | None) -> str:
    if source_url:
        from urllib.parse import urlparse

        parts = urlparse(source_url)
        host = parts.netloc.replace("www.", "").split(".")[0]
        stem = Path(parts.path).stem or path.stem
        return f"{host}-pdf-{slugify(stem)}"
    return f"pdf-{slugify(path.stem)}"


def _normalise_pdf_date(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
    """PDF dates look like D:20250214093000+05'30'."""
    if not raw or not raw.startswith("D:") or len(raw) < 10:
        return None
    digits = raw[2:10]
    if not digits.isdigit():
        return None
    return f"{digits[:4]}-{digits[4:6]}-{digits[6:8]}"

"""Build a document's heading hierarchy from markdown.

This is the foundation of the "structure-aware" claim in the project abstract.
Chunking in Phase 4 splits *within* these sections and never across them, so a
chunk can always be traced back to a real heading path rather than to an
arbitrary character offset.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from rag.ingestion.models import Section

_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*$", re.M)
_CODE_FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^```", re.M)


def sections_from_markdown(markdown: str, root_title: str = "") -> list[Section]:
    """Split markdown into Sections, preserving heading nesting.

    Text appearing before the first heading becomes a preamble section, so no
    content is ever silently dropped. `section_path` is the breadcrumb shown to
    the user in a citation.
    """
    markdown = _blank_out_fenced_code_headings(markdown)
    matches = list(_HEADING_RE.finditer(markdown))

    sections: list[Section] = []
    open_stack: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (level, index in `sections`)

    def path_for(level: int, heading: str) -> tuple[str, int | None]:
        while open_stack and open_stack[-1][0] >= level:
            open_stack.pop()
        parent_index = open_stack[-1][1] if open_stack else None
        ancestors = [sections[i].heading for _, i in open_stack]
        trail = [*ancestors, heading]
        if root_title and (not trail or trail[0] != root_title):
            trail = [root_title, *trail]
        return " > ".join(trail), parent_index

    # Preamble: content before the first heading.
    first_start = matches[0].start() if matches else len(markdown)
    preamble = markdown[:first_start].strip()
    if preamble:
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=root_title or "Introduction",
                level=1,
                content=preamble,
                order_index=0,
                section_path=root_title or "Introduction",
            )
        )

    for i, match in enumerate(matches):
        level = len(match.group(1))
        heading = match.group(2).strip()
        body_start = match.end()
        body_end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(markdown)
        content = markdown[body_start:body_end].strip()

        section_path, parent_index = path_for(level, heading)
        index = len(sections)
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=heading,
                level=level,
                content=content,
                order_index=index,
                section_path=section_path,
                parent_index=parent_index,
            )
        )
        open_stack.append((level, index))

    if not sections and markdown.strip():
        sections.append(
            Section(
                heading=root_title or "Document",
                level=1,
                content=markdown.strip(),
                order_index=0,
                section_path=root_title or "Document",
            )
        )
    return sections


def _blank_out_fenced_code_headings(markdown: str) -> str:
    """Stop '#' inside a fenced code block being read as a heading."""
    if "```" not in markdown:
        return markdown
    out: list[str] = []
    inside = False
    for line in markdown.splitlines():
        if _CODE_FENCE_RE.match(line):
            inside = not inside
            out.append(line)
        elif inside and line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            out.append(line.replace("#", "⌗", 1))
        else:
            out.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out)

"""robots.txt compliance.

Uses the standard library's RobotFileParser — no dependency, and it is the
same implementation most well-behaved crawlers rely on. The crawler consults
this before every fetch, and the effective delay is the larger of the site's
stated Crawl-delay and our own configured floor. We are a guest on someone
else's server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import urllib.robotparser
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

import httpx


@dataclass
class RobotsPolicy:
    """Per-host robots.txt rules, fetched once and cached for the run."""

    user_agent: str
    default_delay: float = 1.0
    timeout: float = 10.0
    _parsers: dict[str, urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser | None] = field(default_factory=dict)
    _sitemaps: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def _parser_for(self, url: str) -> urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser | None:
        host = _host_root(url)
        if host in self._parsers:
            return self._parsers[host]

        robots_url = urljoin(host, "/robots.txt")
        parser: urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser | None = urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser()
        assert parser is not None
        parser.set_url(robots_url)

        try:
            response = httpx.get(
                robots_url,
                timeout=self.timeout,
                follow_redirects=True,
                headers={"User-Agent": self.user_agent},
            )
            if response.status_code == 200:
                parser.parse(response.text.splitlines())
                self._sitemaps[host] = _extract_sitemaps(response.text)
            else:
                # No robots.txt is permission to crawl politely, not a failure.
                parser.parse([])
                self._sitemaps[host] = []
        except httpx.HTTPError:
            # Unreachable robots.txt is treated as "disallow nothing, but be
            # extra careful": we still apply our own rate limit and page cap.
            parser.parse([])
            self._sitemaps[host] = []

        self._parsers[host] = parser
        return parser

    def can_fetch(self, url: str) -> bool:
        parser = self._parser_for(url)
        if parser is None:
            return True
        return bool(parser.can_fetch(self.user_agent, url))

    def delay_for(self, url: str) -> float:
        """The larger of the site's Crawl-delay and our configured floor."""
        parser = self._parser_for(url)
        if parser is None:
            return self.default_delay
        try:
            stated = parser.crawl_delay(self.user_agent)
        except Exception:
            stated = None
        return max(self.default_delay, float(stated)) if stated else self.default_delay

    def sitemaps_for(self, url: str) -> list[str]:
        """Sitemap URLs declared in robots.txt, if any."""
        self._parser_for(url)
        return self._sitemaps.get(_host_root(url), [])


def _host_root(url: str) -> str:
    parts = urlparse(url)
    return f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"


def _extract_sitemaps(robots_text: str) -> list[str]:
    found: list[str] = []
    for line in robots_text.splitlines():
        if line.lower().startswith("sitemap:"):
            value = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
            if value:
                found.append(value)
    return found

"""The orchestrator: assembles a pipeline from a PipelineConfig and runs it.

Every configuration, C0 through C5, runs through this one class. The stages it
builds differ; the sequence, the context assembly, the prompt format and the
logging do not. That is what makes the Chapter 4 numbers attributable — a
difference between two runs is a difference in the stages the config selected,
because nothing else varied.

A configuration whose stages are not built yet is refused rather than silently
approximated. Running "C3" today and getting C0's behaviour would put a wrong
number in the report under a right-looking label, which is worse than an error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from rag.agentic.graph import AgenticRetriever
from rag.chunking.base import Chunk, Chunker
from rag.chunking.fixed import FixedSizeChunker
from rag.chunking.semantic import StructureAwareChunker
from rag.config import (
    ChunkingStrategy,
    PipelineConfig,
    RetrievalStrategy,
    implemented_configs,
)
from rag.embedding.base import Embedder
from rag.generation.base import GenerationResult, Generator
from rag.generation.prompts import (
    REFUSAL_TEXT,
    AssembledContext,
    assemble_context,
    build_prompt,
    format_sources,
)
from rag.indexing.base import VectorIndex
from rag.indexing.bm25 import BM25Index
from rag.ingestion.models import ParsedDocument
from rag.reranking.cross_encoder import CrossEncoderReranker
from rag.retrieval.base import RetrievalResult, stage_timer
from rag.retrieval.dense import DenseRetriever
from rag.retrieval.hybrid import HybridRetriever
from rag.verification.base import VerificationResult, Verifier
from rag.verification.claim_check import ClaimVerifier


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Answer:
    """One answered question, with everything needed to explain or score it."""

    question: str
    answer: str
    config_name: str
    model_name: str

    context: AssembledContext | None = None
    retrieval: RetrievalResult | None = None

    verification: VerificationResult | None = None
    """Populated only by C5. None for every earlier configuration, so a C5 row
    is distinguishable from a C4 row by its presence -- the same convention
    `RetrievalResult.stop_reason` follows for C4."""

    latency_ms: float = 0.0
    generation_ms: float = 0.0
    retrieval_ms: float = 0.0
    prompt_tokens: int | None = None
    completion_tokens: int | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def sources(self) -> list[Any]:
        return self.context.sources if self.context else []

    @property
    def used_demo_sources(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.context and self.context.contains_demo)

    def format(self) -> str:
        parts = (
            [self.answer, "", format_sources(self.context)]
            if self.context
            else [self.answer]
        )
        note = self._verification_note()
        if note:
            parts += ["", note]

        parts.append("")
        parts.append(
            f"[{self.config_name} | {self.model_name} | "
            f"retrieval {self.retrieval_ms:.0f}ms, generation {self.generation_ms:.0f}ms]"
        )
        return "\n".join(parts)

    def _verification_note(self) -> str:
        """What C5 tells the reader, if anything.

        A refusal says what was withheld and shows the withheld text. Silently
        replacing an answer would make C5 unauditable: a reader could not tell
        whether it suppressed a hallucination or destroyed a good answer, and
        that is exactly the question a refusal invites.
        """
        v = self.verification
        if v is None:
            return ""

        if v.refused:
            return (
                "  VERIFICATION: no sentence of the generated answer was supported "
                "by its cited sources, so the answer was withheld.\n"
                f"  Withheld text: {v.original_answer.strip()}"
            )
        if v.unsupported:
            listed = ", ".join(str(n) for n in v.unsupported)
            rate = v.support_rate
            return (
                f"  VERIFICATION: sentence(s) {listed} of {v.checked} were not "
                f"supported by the cited sources"
                + (f" ({rate:.0%} supported)." if rate is not None else ".")
            )
        if v.verdict.value == "unparseable":
            return (
                "  VERIFICATION: the check could not be read, so the answer is "
                "shown unchanged and unverified."
            )
        return ""

    def to_log(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "question": self.question,
            "config": self.config_name,
            "model": self.model_name,
            "latency_ms": round(self.latency_ms, 1),
            "retrieval_ms": round(self.retrieval_ms, 1),
            "generation_ms": round(self.generation_ms, 1),
            "sources": [h.chunk_id for h in self.sources],
            "used_demo_sources": self.used_demo_sources,
            "retrieval": self.retrieval.to_log() if self.retrieval else None,
            "verification": (self.verification.to_log() if self.verification else None),
        }


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Prepared:
    """The state of an answer just before the model is called.

    Exists so `ask()` and the API's streaming path share one retrieval and one
    prompt. A portal answer that differed from the measured one would make
    Chapter 4 describe a system the user never used.
    """

    question: str
    retrieval: RetrievalResult
    context: AssembledContext
    system: str
    prompt: str
    retrieval_ms: float


@dataclass(slots=True)
class IndexReport:
    documents: int = 0
    chunks: int = 0
    indexed: int = 0
    skipped_empty: int = 0
    elapsed_s: float = 0.0

    def summary(self) -> str:
        rate = self.chunks / self.elapsed_s if self.elapsed_s else 0.0
        return (
            f"indexed {self.indexed} chunks from {self.documents} documents "
            f"in {self.elapsed_s:.1f}s ({rate:.0f} chunks/s)"
            + (
                f", {self.skipped_empty} document(s) had no content"
                if self.skipped_empty
                else ""
            )
        )


class Pipeline:
    """Chunk, embed, index, retrieve, rerank, generate — driven by a PipelineConfig."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: PipelineConfig,
        embedder: Embedder,
        index: VectorIndex,
        generator: Generator,
        sparse_index: BM25Index | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        _require_implemented(config)
        self.config = config
        self.embedder = embedder
        self.index = index
        self.generator = generator
        self.sparse_index = sparse_index

        self.chunker: Chunker = _build_chunker(config)
        self.retriever = _build_retriever(
            config, index, embedder, sparse_index, generator
        )
        self.reranker: CrossEncoderReranker | None = _build_reranker(config)
        self.verifier: Verifier | None = _build_verifier(config, generator)

    # --- Indexing -----------------------------------------------------

    def index_documents(
        self, documents: list[ParsedDocument], batch_size: int = 64
    ) -> IndexReport:
        """Chunk, embed and index. Embedding is batched because it dominates."""
        report = IndexReport(documents=len(documents))
        started = time.perf_counter()

        pending: list[Chunk] = []
        for document in documents:
            chunks = self.chunker.chunk(document)
            if not chunks:
                report.skipped_empty += 1
                continue
            report.chunks += len(chunks)
            pending.extend(chunks)

            while len(pending) >= batch_size:
                report.indexed += self._flush(pending[:batch_size])
                del pending[:batch_size]

        if pending:
            report.indexed += self._flush(pending)

        report.elapsed_s = time.perf_counter() - started
        return report

    def _flush(self, chunks: list[Chunk]) -> int:
        vectors = self.embedder.embed_documents([chunk.content for chunk in chunks])
        indexed = self.index.add(chunks, vectors)
        if self.sparse_index is not None:
            self.sparse_index.add(chunks)
        return indexed

    # --- Answering ----------------------------------------------------

    def prepare(self, question: str) -> Prepared:
        """Everything up to the point of generation.

        Split out of `ask()` so the streaming path in the API can reuse it
        rather than reimplementing retrieval. That reuse is not a convenience:
        if the portal assembled its context or built its prompt even slightly
        differently, the answers a user sees would not be the answers Chapter 4
        measured, and no amount of care elsewhere would make them comparable
        again. One implementation, two callers.
        """
        retrieval = self.retriever.retrieve(question, top_k=self.config.dense_top_k)

        context_hits = retrieval.hits
        if self.reranker is not None:
            with stage_timer(retrieval, "rerank"):
                reranked = self.reranker.rerank(
                    question, retrieval.hits, top_n=self.config.rerank_top_n
                )
            retrieval.reranked_hits = reranked
            context_hits = reranked

        context = assemble_context(
            context_hits, max_chars=self.config.max_context_chars
        )
        system, prompt = build_prompt(
            question, context, enforce_citations=self.config.enforce_citations
        )
        return Prepared(
            question=question,
            retrieval=retrieval,
            context=context,
            system=system,
            prompt=prompt,
            retrieval_ms=sum(retrieval.stage_latencies.values()),
        )

    def finish(
        self, prepared: Prepared, generated: GenerationResult, started: float
    ) -> Answer:
        """Verification and assembly, shared by the blocking and streaming paths."""
        answer_text = generated.answer
        verification = None
        if self.verifier is not None:
            verification = self.verifier.verify(
                prepared.question, answer_text, prepared.context
            )
            if verification.refused:
                answer_text = REFUSAL_TEXT

        return Answer(
            question=prepared.question,
            answer=answer_text,
            config_name=self.config.name,
            model_name=generated.model_name,
            context=prepared.context,
            retrieval=prepared.retrieval,
            verification=verification,
            latency_ms=(time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000,
            generation_ms=generated.latency_ms,
            retrieval_ms=prepared.retrieval_ms,
            prompt_tokens=generated.prompt_tokens,
            completion_tokens=generated.completion_tokens,
            metadata={
                "innovations": self.config.innovations_enabled,
                "context_chunks": prepared.context.included,
                "context_dropped": prepared.context.dropped_for_budget,
            },
        )

    def ask(self, question: str) -> Answer:
        """Answer one question. The path every Chapter 4 number came from."""
        started = time.perf_counter()
        prepared = self.prepare(question)

        # C5's check happens inside `finish`. Generation here is byte-for-byte
        # C4's -- same context, same prompt, same call -- so a C4-to-C5
        # difference is the verification and nothing else.
        generated = self.generator.generate(prepared.prompt, system=prepared.system)
        return self.finish(prepared, generated, started)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _require_implemented(config: PipelineConfig) -> None:
    available = implemented_configs()
    if config.name in available:
        return
    missing = ", ".join(config.innovations_enabled) or "features"
    raise NotImplementedError(
        f"Configuration {config.name} requires {missing}, which are not built yet. "
        f"Implemented today: {', '.join(available)}. Running it would produce "
        f"{available[0]}'s behaviour under {config.name}'s name, which would put a "
        f"wrong number in the evaluation."
    )


def _build_chunker(config: PipelineConfig) -> Chunker:
    if config.chunking is ChunkingStrategy.FIXED:
        return FixedSizeChunker(
            size=config.chunk_size_chars, overlap=config.chunk_overlap_chars
        )
    if config.chunking is ChunkingStrategy.STRUCTURE_AWARE:
        return StructureAwareChunker(
            max_size=config.chunk_max_tokens * 4,
            overlap=config.chunk_overlap_chars,
        )
    raise NotImplementedError(
        f"chunking strategy '{config.chunking.value}' arrives in Phase 4"
    )


def _build_verifier(config: PipelineConfig, generator: Generator) -> Verifier | None:
    """C5's verifier, or nothing.

    Deliberately given the *generator's* model rather than the evaluation
    judge. The verifier is part of the system under test; the judge scores that
    system from outside. Wiring the judge in here would put the examiner inside
    the thing being examined, and no Chapter 4 number computed that way would
    mean what it appears to mean.
    """
    if not config.verify_answer:
        return None
    return ClaimVerifier(generator=generator)


def _build_retriever(
    config: PipelineConfig,
    index: VectorIndex,
    embedder: Embedder,
    sparse_index: BM25Index | None,
    generator: Generator,
) -> DenseRetriever | HybridRetriever | AgenticRetriever:
    """Build the retriever the configuration asks for.

    C4 does not replace the retriever — it WRAPS it. The agent runs whatever
    retrieval strategy the config already selected (hybrid, for C4), several
    times, and returns the accumulated pool. Reranking, context assembly,
    prompt and generation downstream are then byte-for-byte the C3 path, which
    is what keeps the ablation single-variable.
    """
    base = _build_base_retriever(config, index, embedder, sparse_index)

    if config.agentic:
        return AgenticRetriever(
            retriever=base,
            generator=generator,
            max_iterations=config.agent_max_iterations,
        )
    return base


def _build_base_retriever(
    config: PipelineConfig,
    index: VectorIndex,
    embedder: Embedder,
    sparse_index: BM25Index | None,
) -> DenseRetriever | HybridRetriever:
    if config.retrieval is RetrievalStrategy.DENSE:
        return DenseRetriever(
            index=index,
            embedder=embedder,
            include_demo_sources=config.include_demo_sources,
        )
    if config.retrieval is RetrievalStrategy.HYBRID:
        if sparse_index is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "hybrid retrieval requires a sparse_index, but none was built. "
                "This is a factory wiring bug, not a missing feature."
            )
        return HybridRetriever(
            index=index,
            sparse_index=sparse_index,
            embedder=embedder,
            dense_top_k=config.dense_top_k,
            sparse_top_k=config.sparse_top_k,
            rrf_k=config.rrf_k,
            include_demo_sources=config.include_demo_sources,
        )
    raise NotImplementedError(
        f"retrieval strategy '{config.retrieval.value}' arrives in Phase 4"
    )


def _build_reranker(config: PipelineConfig) -> CrossEncoderReranker | None:
    if not config.rerank:
        return None
    return CrossEncoderReranker()


__all__ = ["Answer", "IndexReport", "Pipeline"]

"""Reranking strategies.

`CrossEncoderReranker` (Phase 4, C3) rescores C2's fused top-N candidates
jointly with the query, which neither the dense nor the BM25 arm can do on
their own.
"""

from rag.reranking.cross_encoder import CrossEncoderReranker

__all__ = ["CrossEncoderReranker"]

"""C3's reranker: a cross-encoder rescoring C2's fused candidate set.

Dense and BM25 both score a chunk against a query independently of each
other, without ever looking at the query and the chunk together. A
cross-encoder does exactly that: it takes the (query, chunk) pair jointly and
produces a single relevance score, which is a strictly more informed judgment
than fusing two independent rankings -- at the cost of being too slow to run
over an entire corpus, which is why it only reranks C2's already-narrowed
top-N fused candidates, not the whole index.

`cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` is used deliberately: it is small
(~80MB, CPU-friendly, no GPU required), which matches the project's 8GB-RAM
baseline hardware constraint from Report Table 3.1 the same way BM25 was
chosen over a heavier sparse method.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from rag.indexing.base import IndexedHit


class CrossEncoderReranker:
    """Rescores a candidate list jointly with the query; returns the top N."""

    name = "cross_encoder"

    def __init__(
        self, model_name: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2"
    ) -> None:
        self.model_name = model_name
        self._model: Any | None = None

    @property
    def model(self) -> Any:
        if self._model is None:
            from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

            self._model = CrossEncoder(self.model_name)
        return self._model

    def rerank(
        self, query: str, hits: list[IndexedHit], top_n: int
    ) -> list[IndexedHit]:
        if not hits:
            return []

        pairs = [(query, hit.content) for hit in hits]
        scores = self.model.predict(pairs)

        scored = sorted(
            zip(hits, scores, strict=True), key=lambda pair: pair[1], reverse=True
        )

        reranked: list[IndexedHit] = []
        for hit, score in scored[:top_n]:
            reranked.append(
                IndexedHit(
                    chunk_id=hit.chunk_id,
                    content=hit.content,
                    score=float(score),
                    metadata=hit.metadata,
                )
            )
        return reranked

"""The retrieval protocol and its result.

`RetrievalResult` carries per-stage candidate lists and timings, not just the
final hits. That is deliberate: it is what `retrieval_logs` persists, and every
ablation number in Chapter 4 is a query over those rows. A retriever that
returned only its winners would make the comparison unmeasurable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

from rag.indexing.base import IndexedHit


@dataclass(slots=True)
class RetrievalResult:
    """What retrieval produced, and how it got there."""

    query: str
    hits: list[IndexedHit] = field(default_factory=list)

    rewritten_queries: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    dense_hits: list[IndexedHit] = field(default_factory=list)
    sparse_hits: list[IndexedHit] = field(default_factory=list)
    fused_hits: list[IndexedHit] = field(default_factory=list)
    reranked_hits: list[IndexedHit] = field(default_factory=list)

    filters_applied: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    stage_latencies: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    iteration_count: int = 1

    # --- Populated only by the C4 agent ---
    iterations: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    """Round-by-round detail. Empty for every single-pass configuration, so a
    C4 row in retrieval_logs is distinguishable from a C3 row by its presence."""

    stop_reason: str | None = None
    """Why the agent loop ended. Three of its five values mean C4 degraded
    towards C3 for that question, so it is recorded rather than left to be
    inferred from an averaged score."""

    def to_log(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Shaped for the `retrieval_logs` row."""

        def serialise(hits: list[IndexedHit]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
            return [
                {
                    "chunk_id": hit.chunk_id,
                    "score": round(hit.score, 6),
                    "document_id": hit.document_id,
                    "is_demo": hit.is_demo,
                }
                for hit in hits
            ]

        return {
            "original_query": self.query,
            "rewritten_queries": self.rewritten_queries,
            "dense_hits": serialise(self.dense_hits),
            "sparse_hits": serialise(self.sparse_hits),
            "fused_hits": serialise(self.fused_hits),
            "reranked_hits": serialise(self.reranked_hits),
            "filters_applied": self.filters_applied,
            "stage_latencies": {
                k: round(v, 2) for k, v in self.stage_latencies.items()
            },
            "iteration_count": self.iteration_count,
            "iterations": self.iterations,
            "stop_reason": self.stop_reason,
        }


class Retriever(Protocol):
    name: str

    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int) -> RetrievalResult: ...


class stage_timer:  # noqa: N801 - used as a context manager, reads better lowercase
    """Record how long a retrieval stage took, in milliseconds."""

    def __init__(self, result: RetrievalResult, stage: str) -> None:
        self._result = result
        self._stage = stage
        self._started = 0.0

    def __enter__(self) -> stage_timer:
        self._started = time.perf_counter()
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc: object) -> None:
        elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - self._started) * 1000
        self._result.stage_latencies[self._stage] = elapsed

"""C0's retriever: dense similarity, top-k, nothing else.

No query rewriting, no sparse arm, no fusion, no reranking. Whatever the
embedding model ranks highest is what the generator sees. This is the behaviour
every later configuration is measured against, so it is implemented carefully:
a baseline that is worse than a naive implementation would honestly be inflates
every improvement claimed on top of it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from rag.embedding.base import Embedder
from rag.indexing.base import VectorIndex
from rag.retrieval.base import RetrievalResult, stage_timer


class DenseRetriever:
    name = "dense"

    def __init__(
        self,
        index: VectorIndex,
        embedder: Embedder,
        include_demo_sources: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.index = index
        self.embedder = embedder
        self.include_demo_sources = include_demo_sources

    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int) -> RetrievalResult:
        result = RetrievalResult(query=query)

        where: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        if not self.include_demo_sources:
            where = {"is_demo": False}
        result.filters_applied = dict(where or {})

        with stage_timer(result, "embed_query"):
            vector = self.embedder.embed_query(query)

        with stage_timer(result, "dense_search"):
            hits = self.index.search(vector, top_k=top_k, where=where)

        result.dense_hits = hits
        # C0 has no fusion and no reranking, so the dense hits are the final
        # hits. The other lists stay empty, which is exactly what distinguishes
        # a C0 row from a C2 row in retrieval_logs.
        result.hits = hits
        return result

"""C2's retriever: dense and BM25 in parallel, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

Neither arm's ranking is touched by this class -- it only combines two
independently correct rankings into one. RRF is used instead of a weighted
score average because dense cosine similarity and BM25 scores live on
incomparable scales; averaging them would let whichever metric happens to
have larger raw magnitudes quietly dominate the fusion.

This is specifically the fix for a real, verified gap in C0/C1: a chunk that
answers a question in terse, keyword-dense form (a bullet list of
accreditation facts, for instance) can rank far outside a dense retriever's
top-k, because a bullet list does not read as semantically similar to a
natural-language question even when it contains the exact answer. BM25 scores
that same chunk highly on literal term overlap; RRF lets either arm's high
rank pull a chunk into the final result.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from rag.embedding.base import Embedder
from rag.indexing.base import IndexedHit, VectorIndex
from rag.indexing.bm25 import BM25Index
from rag.retrieval.base import RetrievalResult, stage_timer


def reciprocal_rank_fusion(
    ranked_lists: list[list[IndexedHit]], k: int = 60
) -> list[IndexedHit]:
    """Combine multiple rankings by rank position, not by raw score.

    Each hit's contribution is 1 / (k + rank). A chunk near the top of
    *either* list scores well; one near the top of both scores best of all.
    `k` dampens how much rank 1 outweighs rank 2 -- 60 is RRF's usual default
    and matches PipelineConfig.rrf_k, so C2's behaviour is exactly what the
    config declares, not a hidden second constant.
    """
    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
    best_hit: dict[str, IndexedHit] = {}

    for ranked in ranked_lists:
        for rank, hit in enumerate(ranked, start=1):
            scores[hit.chunk_id] = scores.get(hit.chunk_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (k + rank)
            if hit.chunk_id not in best_hit:
                best_hit[hit.chunk_id] = hit

    ordered_ids = sorted(scores, key=lambda cid: scores[cid], reverse=True)
    fused: list[IndexedHit] = []
    for cid in ordered_ids:
        hit = best_hit[cid]
        fused.append(
            IndexedHit(
                chunk_id=hit.chunk_id,
                content=hit.content,
                score=scores[cid],
                metadata=hit.metadata,
            )
        )
    return fused


class HybridRetriever:
    """Dense + BM25 in parallel, fused with RRF."""

    name = "hybrid"

    def __init__(
        self,
        index: VectorIndex,
        sparse_index: BM25Index,
        embedder: Embedder,
        dense_top_k: int = 20,
        sparse_top_k: int = 20,
        rrf_k: int = 60,
        include_demo_sources: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.index = index
        self.sparse_index = sparse_index
        self.embedder = embedder
        self.dense_top_k = dense_top_k
        self.sparse_top_k = sparse_top_k
        self.rrf_k = rrf_k
        self.include_demo_sources = include_demo_sources

    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int) -> RetrievalResult:
        result = RetrievalResult(query=query)

        where: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        if not self.include_demo_sources:
            where = {"is_demo": False}
        result.filters_applied = dict(where or {})

        with stage_timer(result, "embed_query"):
            vector = self.embedder.embed_query(query)

        with stage_timer(result, "dense_search"):
            dense_hits = self.index.search(vector, top_k=self.dense_top_k, where=where)

        with stage_timer(result, "sparse_search"):
            sparse_hits = self.sparse_index.search(
                query, top_k=self.sparse_top_k, where=where
            )

        with stage_timer(result, "fuse"):
            fused = reciprocal_rank_fusion([dense_hits, sparse_hits], k=self.rrf_k)

        result.dense_hits = dense_hits
        result.sparse_hits = sparse_hits
        result.fused_hits = fused[:top_k]
        result.hits = result.fused_hits
        return result

"""Answering as a sequence of events, for the portal.

`Pipeline.ask()` returns an answer after between 60 and 330 seconds depending
on the configuration, and on the measured hardware most of that is spent before
the first token exists: under C4 and C5, retrieval alone averages 95-105 s.
Token streaming on its own would therefore leave a user watching nothing at all
for the first minute and a half, which reads as a hung page rather than a
thinking one.

So this yields *stage* events too. What the agent is doing is genuinely
interesting -- it searched again, it found eleven new passages, it decided it
had enough -- and surfacing it turns the system's biggest weakness, its
latency, into the thing that makes it legible.

The design rule this module follows: **it never re-implements a pipeline
stage.** It calls `Pipeline.prepare()` and `Pipeline.finish()`, the same
methods `ask()` uses. If the portal assembled context or built prompts of its
own, portal answers would drift from the answers Chapter 4 measured, and the
evaluation would describe a system nobody used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from collections.abc import Iterator
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from rag.generation.base import GenerationResult, StreamingGenerator
from rag.pipeline import Answer, Pipeline


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Event:
    """One thing worth telling the client about.

    `name` is the SSE event type; `data` is JSON-serialisable. Deliberately a
    plain record rather than a formatted SSE string, so the transport layer
    owns the wire format and this module stays testable without HTTP.
    """

    name: str
    data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


def answer_events(pipeline: Pipeline, question: str) -> Iterator[Event]:
    """Answer a question as a stream of events.

    Order is fixed and a client may rely on it:

        stage(retrieval) -> [stage(agent) ...] -> stage(context)
        -> sources -> token* -> stage(verification)? -> answer -> done

    `answer` always arrives, and always carries the same text `ask()` would
    have returned -- including a C5 refusal, which replaces text the client has
    already been shown token by token. That is why `answer` is authoritative
    and the tokens are a preview: a client must render the final text, not its
    accumulation of tokens.
    """
    started = time.perf_counter()

    yield Event(
        "stage",
        {"stage": "retrieval", "status": "started", "config": pipeline.config.name},
    )

    prepared = pipeline.prepare(question)
    retrieval = prepared.retrieval

    # The agent's round-by-round record, if this configuration has one. This is
    # the part worth watching: it is the only place a user can see the system
    # decide something.
    for iteration in retrieval.iterations:
        yield Event(
            "stage",
            {
                "stage": "agent",
                "iteration": iteration.get("iteration"),
                "query": iteration.get("query"),
                "new_passages": iteration.get("new_chunks"),
                "decision": iteration.get("decision"),
            },
        )
    if retrieval.stop_reason:
        yield Event(
            "stage",
            {
                "stage": "agent",
                "status": "finished",
                "stop_reason": retrieval.stop_reason,
            },
        )

    yield Event(
        "stage",
        {
            "stage": "retrieval",
            "status": "finished",
            "passages": len(retrieval.hits),
            "reranked_to": len(retrieval.reranked_hits) or None,
            "elapsed_ms": round(prepared.retrieval_ms, 1),
        },
    )

    # Sources before tokens, so citation markers in the streamed text resolve
    # to something the moment they appear.
    yield Event(
        "sources",
        {
            "sources": [
                {
                    "marker": f"[S{position}]",
                    "label": hit.citation_label(),
                    "url": hit.metadata.get("source_url") or None,
                    "page": hit.page_number,
                    "is_demo": hit.is_demo,
                    "chunk_id": hit.chunk_id,
                }
                for position, hit in enumerate(prepared.context.sources, start=1)
            ],
            "contains_demo": prepared.context.contains_demo,
        },
    )

    yield Event("stage", {"stage": "generation", "status": "started"})

    generated = yield from _generate(pipeline, prepared)

    if pipeline.verifier is not None:
        yield Event("stage", {"stage": "verification", "status": "started"})

    answer = pipeline.finish(prepared, generated, started)

    if answer.verification is not None:
        v = answer.verification
        yield Event(
            "stage",
            {
                "stage": "verification",
                "status": "finished",
                "verdict": v.verdict.value,
                "checked": v.checked,
                "unsupported": v.unsupported,
                "support_rate": v.support_rate,
                "refused": v.refused,
            },
        )

    yield Event("answer", _answer_payload(answer))
    yield Event("done", {"latency_ms": round(answer.latency_ms, 1)})


def _generate(pipeline: Pipeline, prepared: Any) -> Iterator[Event]:
    """Stream tokens if the generator can, otherwise produce them in one go.

    The fallback matters: it keeps every event before and after generation
    identical whether or not streaming is available, so a client written
    against this stream works with a non-streaming generator (a test double, a
    future backend) without a second code path.
    """
    generator = pipeline.generator
    if isinstance(generator, StreamingGenerator) and hasattr(generator, "stream"):
        result: GenerationResult | None = None
        for piece in generator.stream(prepared.prompt, system=prepared.system):
            if isinstance(piece, GenerationResult):
                result = piece
            else:
                yield Event("token", {"text": piece})
        if result is None:  # pragma: no cover - a stream that yielded no result
            raise RuntimeError("streaming generator produced no final result")
        return result

    result = generator.generate(prepared.prompt, system=prepared.system)
    yield Event("token", {"text": result.answer})
    return result


def _answer_payload(answer: Answer) -> dict[str, Any]:
    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "answer": answer.answer,
        "config": answer.config_name,
        "model": answer.model_name,
        "used_demo_sources": answer.used_demo_sources,
        "latency_ms": round(answer.latency_ms, 1),
        "retrieval_ms": round(answer.retrieval_ms, 1),
        "generation_ms": round(answer.generation_ms, 1),
    }
    if answer.verification is not None:
        v = answer.verification
        payload["verification"] = {
            "verdict": v.verdict.value,
            "support_rate": v.support_rate,
            "unsupported_sentences": v.unsupported_text,
            "refused": v.refused,
            # What was withheld, so a refusal is auditable in the UI exactly as
            # it is on the command line. Suppressing text invisibly would make
            # C5 unfalsifiable to a reader.
            "withheld_text": v.original_answer if v.refused else None,
        }
    return payload

"""Phase 5: the C4 agentic retrieval loop.

Nothing here imports LangGraph. That is not a workaround — it is the reason
`nodes.py` takes its dependencies as arguments and `graph.py` contains no logic
of its own. The loop's behaviour (what stops it, what it deduplicates, what it
records) is decided entirely by `base.py`, `decide.py` and `nodes.py`, so it is
asserted here against a hand-rolled driver that wires the same three
transitions in the same order the graph does.

What that leaves unverified is stated plainly rather than implied: the
`StateGraph` construction in `build_graph()` itself. It has no branching of its
own, and `TestWiring::test_driver_matches_graph_wiring` pins the shape it must
have, but the compile-and-invoke path runs only on a machine with langgraph
installed.

The parser gets the most attention because it is where this will actually
break. A quantized 7B model asked for one line of output will return that line
wrapped in bold, prefixed with "Answer:", followed by an apology, or replaced
by a paragraph of reasoning — and the dangerous failure is not an exception,
it is a malformed response read leniently as READY, which turns C4 into C3
while still reporting itself as C4.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import inspect

import pytest

from rag.agentic.base import AgentIteration, AgentState, StopReason
from rag.agentic.decide import MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS, build_decide_prompt, parse_decision
from rag.agentic.graph import STATE_KEY, AgenticRetriever
from rag.agentic.nodes import decide_node, retrieve_node, should_continue
from rag.config import C3_RERANK, C4_AGENTIC, implemented_configs
from rag.generation.base import GenerationResult
from rag.indexing.base import IndexedHit
from rag.retrieval.base import RetrievalResult

def _hit(chunk_id: str, content: str = "text", score: float = 1.0) -> IndexedHit:
    return IndexedHit(
        chunk_id=chunk_id,
        content=content,
        score=score,
        metadata={
            "document_id": f"doc-{chunk_id}",
            "document_title": f"Doc {chunk_id}",
        },
    )


class _ScriptedRetriever:
    """Returns a prepared hit list per query, and records what it was asked."""

    name = "scripted"

    def __init__(self, script: dict[str, list[IndexedHit]] | None = None) -> None:
        self.script = script or {}
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
        self.default: list[IndexedHit] = []

    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int) -> RetrievalResult:
        self.calls.append((query, top_k))
        hits = list(self.script.get(query, self.default))
        result = RetrievalResult(query=query, hits=hits)
        # Mimic a hybrid retriever: the arms overlap with each other and with
        # the fused result, which is what the per-arm dedup has to survive.
        result.dense_hits = hits
        result.sparse_hits = list(reversed(hits))
        result.stage_latencies = {"dense_search": 1.0}
        result.filters_applied = {"is_demo": False}
        return result


class _ScriptedGenerator:
    """Emits a prepared decision per call; repeats the last one if exhausted."""

    model_name = "scripted"

    def __init__(self, *replies: str) -> None:
        self.replies = list(replies)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []

    def generate(self, prompt: str, system: str | None = None) -> GenerationResult:
        self.calls.append((prompt, system))
        index = min(len(self.calls) - 1, len(self.replies) - 1)
        reply = self.replies[index] if self.replies else "READY"
        return GenerationResult(
            answer=reply, model_name=self.model_name, latency_ms=1.0
        )


class _DrivenAgent(AgenticRetriever):
    """`AgenticRetriever` with the graph runtime replaced by a plain loop.

    The loop below is deliberately a transcription of `build_graph()`: entry at
    `retrieve`, an unconditional edge to `decide`, then `should_continue` back
    to `retrieve` or out. If those two ever diverge this class is the thing to
    change, and `test_driver_matches_graph_wiring` is the thing that notices.
    """

    def _run(self, state: AgentState) -> AgentState:
        visits = 0
        limit = self.max_iterations * 2 + 4
        while True:
            visits += 1
            if visits > limit:  # pragma: no cover - a runaway loop is a bug
                raise AssertionError("driver exceeded the graph's recursion limit")
            state = retrieve_node(state, self.retriever)
            state = decide_node(state, self.generator)
            if should_continue(state) == "finish":
                return state

class TestParsingTheDecision:
    """The one place a small quantized model reliably misbehaves."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "text",
        [
            "READY",
            "ready",
            "  READY  ",
            "**READY**",
            "READY.",
            "Answer: READY",
            "`ready`",
            "READY\nThe excerpts cover the question.",
        ],
    )
    def test_ready_is_recognised_through_its_wrappers(self, text: str) -> None:
        decision = parse_decision(text)
        assert decision.ready is True
        assert decision.parsed is True
        assert decision.query is None

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("text", "expected"),
        [
            ("SEARCH: placement statistics 2024", "placement statistics 2024"),
            ("search: placement statistics 2024", "placement statistics 2024"),
            ("**SEARCH:** placement statistics", "placement statistics"),
            ("SEARCH - placement statistics", "placement statistics"),
            ("SEARCH:   placement statistics.  ", "placement statistics"),
            ('SEARCH: "placement statistics"', "placement statistics"),
            ("Decision: SEARCH: placement statistics", "placement statistics"),
            (
                "SEARCH: placement statistics because the excerpts omit them",
                "placement statistics",
            ),
            (
                "Some reasoning first.\nSEARCH: placement statistics",
                "placement statistics",
            ),
        ],
    )
    def test_search_queries_survive_the_models_decorations(
        self, text: str, expected: str
    ) -> None:
        decision = parse_decision(text)
        assert decision.parsed is True
        assert decision.ready is False
        assert decision.query == expected

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(

        assert decision.parsed is False
        assert decision.query is None

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["", "   ", "SEARCH:", "SEARCH:   "])
    def test_unreadable_output_is_recorded_not_guessed(self, text: str) -> None:
        """The critical case: never silently interpreted as READY.

        `ready=True` here only means "stop the loop"; `parsed=False` is what
        the stop reason and the log key off, so a model that stopped producing
        usable output cannot be mistaken in the results for a model that was
        satisfied.
        """

        assert decision.parsed is False
        assert decision.label == "UNPARSEABLE"

    def test_ready_takes_precedence_over_a_later_search_line(self) -> None:
        # First readable line wins, matching the "exactly one line" contract.
        assert parse_decision("READY\nSEARCH: more").ready is True
