def seed_reference(session: Session) -> None:
    """Departments, B.Tech programmes and accreditation, from public sources."""
    by_code: dict[str, Department] = {d.code: d for d in session.scalars(select(Department))}

    for row in DEPARTMENTS:
        department = by_code.get(row["code"])
        if department is None:
            department = Department(**row)
            session.add(department)
            by_code[row["code"]] = department
        else:
            for key, value in row.items():
                setattr(department, key, value)
    session.flush()

    # A typo in one intake would otherwise pass unnoticed until someone asked
    # the assistant for the total.
    total = sum(p["intake"] for p in BTECH_PROGRAMS)
    if total != TOTAL_BTECH_INTAKE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"B.Tech intakes sum to {total}, but the bachelors page states "
            f"{TOTAL_BTECH_INTAKE}. Fix app/seed/reference.py before seeding."
        )

    existing_programs = {(p.slug): p for p in session.scalars(select(Program))}
    for row in BTECH_PROGRAMS:
        data = dict(row)
        department = by_code[data.pop("department_code")]
        program = existing_programs.get(data["slug"])
        if program is None:
            session.add(
                Program(
                    department_id=department.id,
                    level=ProgramLevel.BTECH,
                    duration_years=4,
                    source_url="https://www.pce.ac.in/academics/bachelors/",
                    **data,
                )
            )
        else:
            program.department_id = department.id
            for key, value in data.items():
                setattr(program, key, value)

    existing_bodies = {a.body for a in session.scalars(select(Accreditation))}
    for row in ACCREDITATIONS:
        body = AccreditationBody(row["body"])
        if body in existing_bodies:
            continue
        session.add(Accreditation(**{**row, "body": body}))

    session.flush()
    logger.info(
        "seed_reference",
        departments=len(DEPARTMENTS),
        programs=len(BTECH_PROGRAMS),
        total_intake=total,
    )


def seed_admin(session: Session) -> None:
    """Create the admin account, if the configured email is not already taken."""
    from passlib.context import CryptContext

    email = settings.admin_email
    password = settings.admin_password

    if not password or password.startswith("change_this"):
        logger.warning(
            "seed_admin_skipped",
            reason="ADMIN_PASSWORD is unset or still the placeholder in .env",
        )
        return

    if session.scalar(select(User).where(User.email == email)) is not None:
        logger.info("seed_admin", status="already exists", email=email)
        return

    context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto")
    session.add(
        User(
            email=email,
            password_hash=context.hash(password),
            full_name="Administrator",
            role=UserRole.ADMIN,
            is_active=True,
        )
    )
    session.flush()
    logger.info("seed_admin", status="created", email=email)


def seed_corpus(session: Session) -> None:
    """Load the corpus, and refuse to call a partial load a success.

    The seed once loaded 582 of 609 documents and reported it only as a line in
    a skipped list nobody read. A corpus quietly missing 27 documents is a
    retrieval system that quietly cannot answer questions about them, so a
    shortfall now raises.
    """
    corpus_dir = Path(settings.corpus_dir)
    report = load_corpus(session, corpus_dir)
    print(report.summary())

    if report.skipped:
        print(f"\n{len(report.skipped)} document(s) skipped:")
        for line in report.skipped[:15]:
            print(f"  {line}")
        if len(report.skipped) > 15:
            print(f"  ... and {len(report.skipped) - 15} more")

    print(
        f"\nreconciled: manifest {report.manifest_total}, "
        f"loaded {report.accounted_for}, skipped {len(report.skipped)}"
    )
    if not report.is_complete:
        missing = report.manifest_total - report.accounted_for
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{missing} of {report.manifest_total} documents in the manifest did not "
            f"reach the database. The corpus is incomplete, so the load is being "
            f"treated as a failure rather than a partial success. See the skipped "
            f"list above for which documents and why."
        )


def seed_prune(session: Session) -> None:
    """Delete documents the manifest no longer lists.

    Never part of `all`. Every other step only adds, so running `all` twice is
    harmless; this one removes, and a manifest written by a failed parse would
    make it remove real documents. It has to be asked for by name.
    """
    deleted, doc_ids = prune_documents(session, Path(settings.corpus_dir))
    if not deleted:
        print("nothing to prune: every document in the database is in the manifest")
        logger.info("prune", status="already consistent")
        return

    print(f"deleted {deleted} document(s) absent from the manifest:")
    for doc_id in doc_ids[:25]:
        print(f"  {doc_id}")
    if deleted > 25:
        print(f"  ... and {deleted - 25} more")
    logger.warning("prune", deleted=deleted)


def verify(session: Session) -> int:
    """Print what is actually in the database. Run after any seed step."""
    from app.models.knowledge import Document, DocumentSection

    counts = {
        "departments": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Department)),
        "programs": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Program)),
        "accreditations": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Accreditation)),
        "documents": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Document)),
        "document_sections": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(DocumentSection)),
        "users": session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(User)),
    }
    real = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Document).where(~Document.is_demo))
    demo = session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Document).where(Document.is_demo))
    with_pages = session.scalar(
        select(func.count(func.distinct(DocumentSection.document_id))).where(
            DocumentSection.start_page.isnot(None)
        )
    )

    print("\nDatabase contents")
    print("=" * 40)
    width = max(len(k) for k in counts)
    for key, value in counts.items():
        print(f"  {key:<{width}}  {value}")

    total = (real or 0) + (demo or 0)
    if total:
        print(f"\n  real documents      {real}  ({(real or 0) / total:.1%})")
        print(f"  demo documents      {demo}")
        print(f"  with page numbers   {with_pages}")

    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


STEPS = {
    "reference": seed_reference,
    "corpus": seed_corpus,
    "admin": seed_admin,
}

# Steps that must be named explicitly and never ride along on `all`. Everything
# in STEPS only ever adds or updates, which is what makes `all` safe to re-run;
# `prune` deletes, so it is kept out of that set deliberately.
EXPLICIT_STEPS = {
    "prune": seed_prune,
}

ALL_STEPS = {**STEPS, **EXPLICIT_STEPS}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    configure_logging()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m app.seed")
    parser.add_argument(
        "steps",
        nargs="*",
        choices=[*ALL_STEPS, "all"],
        default=["all"],
        help="Which steps to run. Default: all.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    chosen = list(STEPS) if "all" in args.steps or not args.steps else args.steps

    with SessionLocal() as session:
        try:
            for name in chosen:
                print(f"==> {name}")
                ALL_STEPS[name](session)
            session.commit()
        except PruneRefusedError as exc:
            # Not a crash: the refusal is the feature. Say what stopped it
            # without a traceback, so the message is the thing that is read.
            session.rollback()
            print(f"\nPRUNE REFUSED: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        except Exception as exc:
            session.rollback()
            print(f"\nSEED FAILED during '{name}': {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1

        return verify(session)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Load the Phase 1 corpus into PostgreSQL.

Reads `corpus/manifest.json` and `corpus/normalised/*.json` — the outputs of
`python -m rag.ingestion` — and writes `documents`, `document_sections` and
`suppressed_documents`.

Two properties matter more than speed:

**Idempotent.** Keyed on `doc_id`, so running it twice is the same as running
it once. A document whose `content_hash` is unchanged is skipped entirely; one
whose hash has moved has its sections replaced wholesale rather than merged,
because a re-parse can renumber every section and a partial merge would leave
orphans pointing at headings that no longer exist.

**`is_demo` is copied, never inferred.** The value comes from the manifest,
which got it from the parser, which refused to mark an internal-only category
as real. Nothing in this module decides whether a document is demo data; it
only carries the decision forward.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import delete, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models.enums import DocumentCategory, IngestStatus, SourceType
from app.models.institutional import Department
from app.models.knowledge import Document, DocumentSection, SuppressedDocument


@dataclass
class LoadReport:
    manifest_total: int = 0
    inserted: int = 0
    updated: int = 0
    unchanged: int = 0
    suppressed: int = 0
    sections: int = 0
    skipped: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def accounted_for(self) -> int:
        """Documents this run actually put in, or confirmed already in, the DB."""
        return self.inserted + self.updated + self.unchanged

    @property
    def is_complete(self) -> bool:
        return self.accounted_for == self.manifest_total

    def summary(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"documents: {self.inserted} inserted, {self.updated} updated, "
            f"{self.unchanged} unchanged | sections: {self.sections} | "
            f"suppressed rows: {self.suppressed}"
        )


def load_corpus(session: Session, corpus_dir: Path) -> LoadReport:
    """Load manifest + normalised documents. Returns what changed."""
    manifest_path = corpus_dir / "manifest.json"
    if not manifest_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{manifest_path} not found. Run `python -m rag.ingestion parse` and "
            f"`... manifest` before seeding."
        )

    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    normalised_dir = corpus_dir / "normalised"
    report = LoadReport(manifest_total=len(manifest.get("documents", [])))

    departments = {d.name: d.id for d in session.scalars(select(Department))}

    for row in manifest.get("documents", []):
        _load_one(session, row, normalised_dir, departments, report)

    report.suppressed = _load_suppressed(session, manifest.get("suppressed_duplicates", []))
    session.flush()
    return report


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _load_one(
    session: Session,
    row: dict[str, Any],
    normalised_dir: Path,
    departments: dict[str, Any],
    report: LoadReport,
) -> None:
    doc_id = row["doc_id"]
    existing = session.scalar(select(Document).where(Document.doc_id == doc_id))

    if existing is not None and existing.content_hash == row["content_hash"]:
        report.unchanged += 1
        return

    payload = _read_normalised(normalised_dir, doc_id, row.get("file_stem"))
    if payload is None:
        report.skipped.append(
            f"{doc_id}: no normalised .json on disk "
            f"(looked for {row.get('file_stem') or '<derived stem>'}.json)"
        )
        return

    fields = _document_fields(row, payload, departments)

    if existing is None:
        document = Document(doc_id=doc_id, **fields)
        session.add(document)
        session.flush()
        report.inserted += 1
    else:
        for key, value in fields.items():
            setattr(existing, key, value)
        # Replace rather than merge: a re-parse can renumber every section, and
        # merging would leave rows pointing at headings that no longer exist.
        session.execute(delete(DocumentSection).where(DocumentSection.document_id == existing.id))
        session.flush()
        document = existing
        report.updated += 1

    report.sections += _load_sections(session, document, payload.get("sections", []))


def _document_fields(
    row: dict[str, Any], payload: dict[str, Any], departments: dict[str, Any]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "title": (row.get("title") or payload.get("title") or "Untitled")[:500],
        "source_type": SourceType(row["source_type"]),
        "category": _category(row.get("category")),
        "source_url": row.get("source_url"),
        "local_path": row.get("local_path"),
        "fetched_at": _datetime(row.get("fetched_at")),
        "content_hash": row["content_hash"],
        "department_id": departments.get(row.get("department") or ""),
        "author": payload.get("author"),
        "published_date": _date(row.get("published_date")),
        "page_count": row.get("page_count"),
        "word_count": row.get("word_count"),
        "language": payload.get("language") or "en",
        "ingest_status": IngestStatus.PARSED,
        # Copied from the manifest. Never inferred here.
        "is_demo": bool(row.get("is_demo", False)),
        "demo_reason": row.get("demo_reason"),
    }


def _load_sections(session: Session, document: Document, sections: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """Insert sections, then wire up parents in a second pass.

    Two passes because a section's parent may appear after it in the list, and
    the foreign key needs a row that already exists.
    """
    created: list[DocumentSection] = []
    for payload in sections:
        section = DocumentSection(
            document_id=document.id,
            heading=payload.get("heading") or "",
            level=int(payload.get("level") or 1),
            section_path=payload.get("section_path") or "",
            order_index=int(payload.get("order_index") or len(created)),
            content=payload.get("content"),
            char_count=len(payload.get("content") or ""),
            start_page=payload.get("start_page"),
            end_page=payload.get("end_page"),
        )
        session.add(section)
        created.append(section)

    session.flush()

    for payload, section in zip(sections, created, strict=True):
        parent_index = payload.get("parent_index")
        if parent_index is not None and 0 <= int(parent_index) < len(created):
            section.parent_section_id = created[int(parent_index)].id

    session.flush()
    return len(created)


def _load_suppressed(session: Session, rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """Record the duplicates the pipeline dropped.

    A suppressed page must still be answerable as "yes, we crawled it", so the
    URL survives here even though its content does not.
    """
    if not rows:
        return 0

    existing = {d.doc_id for d in session.scalars(select(SuppressedDocument))}
    added = 0
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("doc_id") in existing:
            continue
        session.add(
            SuppressedDocument(
                doc_id=row["doc_id"],
                title=(row.get("title") or "")[:500] or None,
                source_url=row.get("source_url"),
                duplicate_of_doc_id=row["duplicate_of"],
                content_hash=row.get("content_hash") or "",
            )
        )
        added += 1
    return added


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsing helpers — tolerant, because a bad field should skip a document rather
# than abort a load of eight hundred.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _read_normalised(
    normalised_dir: Path, doc_id: str, file_stem: str | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Find a document's .json by the stem the pipeline actually wrote it under.

    `file_stem` comes from the manifest. It is passed in rather than derived
    because doc_id -> filename is lossy: slugify truncates at 80 characters, so
    re-deriving it produces the wrong name for any longer id. An earlier version
    of this function did re-derive it, without the truncation, and silently
    skipped all 27 documents whose doc_id exceeded 80 characters.

    The fallback exists only for manifests written before `file_stem` was
    recorded, and it calls the pipeline's own slugify rather than
    reimplementing it — the whole point being that this transformation is
    defined in exactly one place.
    """
    if not file_stem:
        from rag.ingestion.models import slugify

        file_stem = slugify(doc_id.replace("/", "-"))

    path = normalised_dir / f"{file_stem}.json"
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    try:
        return dict(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None


def _category(value: str | None) -> DocumentCategory:
    try:
        return DocumentCategory(value or "other")
    except ValueError:
        return DocumentCategory.OTHER


def _datetime(value: str | None) -> datetime | None:
    if not value:
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _date(value: str | None) -> date | None:
    if not value:
        return None
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value[:10])
    except ValueError:
        return None


__all__ = ["LoadReport", "load_corpus"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pruning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class PruneRefusedError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised rather than deleting documents on evidence that looks wrong."""


def prune_documents(session: Session, corpus_dir: Path) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    """Delete documents the manifest no longer lists. Returns (deleted, doc_ids).

    `load_corpus` inserts and updates but never deletes, and nothing else does
    either, so a document that leaves the corpus keeps its database row for
    ever. The rows then outlive the index that was built from the manifest, and
    the portal lists documents that retrieval cannot cite.

    Deleting is the dangerous direction, so this refuses in the two cases where
    the evidence for a deletion is not trustworthy:

    * **The manifest is not a superset of the database's loaded set.** If the
      manifest lists documents the database has not got, the two were not
      produced from the same load, and a difference in the other direction says
      nothing about what should be removed. Run `corpus` first.
    * **The deletion is implausibly large.** A truncated or half-written
      manifest would otherwise take most of a working corpus with it. One in
      five is well past any real corpus revision and reads as a broken input.

    Sections and chunks carry `ondelete="CASCADE"`, so the database removes
    them; nothing here has to walk the children.
    """
    manifest_path = corpus_dir / "manifest.json"
    try:
        raw = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise PruneRefusedError(f"cannot read {manifest_path}: {exc}") from exc

    manifest_ids = {d["doc_id"] for d in raw.get("documents", []) if d.get("doc_id")}
    if not manifest_ids:
        raise PruneRefusedError(f"{manifest_path} lists no documents; refusing to prune")

    database_ids = set(session.scalars(select(Document.doc_id)))
    orphans = sorted(database_ids - manifest_ids)
    absent = manifest_ids - database_ids

    if absent:
        raise PruneRefusedError(
            f"{len(absent)} document(s) in the manifest are not in the database. "
            f"The two are not from the same load, so the extra rows cannot be "
            f"assumed stale. Run `python -m app.seed corpus` first."
        )

    if not orphans:
        return 0, []

    if database_ids and len(orphans) > len(database_ids) * 0.2:
        raise PruneRefusedError(
            f"{len(orphans)} of {len(database_ids)} documents are absent from the "
            f"manifest. That is too large a share to be a corpus revision and looks "
            f"like a truncated manifest. Nothing was deleted; check "
            f"{manifest_path} before forcing this through."
        )

    session.execute(delete(Document).where(Document.doc_id.in_(orphans)))
    return len(orphans), orphans

"""Verified institutional reference data.

Everything in this module was read from a public page on pce.ac.in and is
recorded with the URL it came from. It is hard-coded rather than scraped
because it is small, slow-changing, structural data that the portal's pages are
built around — and because a wrong intake number is the kind of error an
examiner will notice immediately, so it is worth having it pinned, sourced and
reviewable in one file rather than inferred from HTML on every run.

Anything NOT confirmed from a public page does not belong here. If a figure is
needed that the institute has not published, it goes in `corpus/demo/` with a
`demo_reason`, not in this file with a guess.

Sources:
    https://www.pce.ac.in/about/the-institute/
    https://www.pce.ac.in/academics/bachelors/

"""Reading the evaluation runs off disk.

The harness writes, per configuration, a `summary.csv` and one `qNN.txt` per
question. Those files are what Chapter 4 cites, so they are the authority.
Nothing here copies them into a table — a database copy would be a second
source of truth able to disagree with the evidence, which is the failure this
project has spent two phases chasing elsewhere.

**The runs are not uniform, and that shaped this module.** `--json` was added
to the harness partway through data collection, so C0, C4 and C5 have a full
JSON log appended to each answer — sources, per-stage latencies, agent
iterations, verification — while C1, C1-CONTROL, C2 and C3 have only the answer
text. `summary.csv` is the one thing every run has, and it carries the question
and the timings, so it is read first and the log is treated as extra detail
where it exists.

The alternative was to expose only the three configurations with logs, which
would have quietly dropped C3 — the portal default and the headline of the
ablation — from the comparison. Better to serve every run and say which parts
of each were recorded.

One module rather than one reader per route: `/admin/evaluations` and the
public comparison parse the same files, and two parsers over one format drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

# Mounted read-only at /app/eval by docker-compose. Before that mount existed
# this pointed at a path absent from the image, and the endpoints reported "no
# results directory" — which reads as an empty evaluation rather than a missing
# volume.
EVAL_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("EVAL_RESULTS_DIR", "/app/eval/results"))

_QUESTION_FILE = re.compile(r"^q\d+$")

# The harness writes each answer as:
#
#     <answer text>
#
#     Sources:
#       [S1] <citation label>
#             <url>
#
#       N retrieved chunk(s) omitted for context budget.
#
#     [C3 | model | retrieval 12683ms, generation 15737ms]
#
# followed, in the runs made after `--json` was added, by a JSON log.
#
# The sources are parsed from this block rather than from the log's `sources`
# field, which holds bare chunk ids. The block has the citation label and the
# URL — what a reader needs — and unlike the log it exists in every run.
_SOURCES_HEADING = "\nSources:"
_SOURCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*\[S(\d+)\]\s*(.+?)\s*$")
_URL_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s+(https?://\S+)\s*$")
_OMITTED_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+)\s+retrieved chunk")
_TRAILER_LINE = re.compile(r"^\[[^|\]]+\|[^\]]*\]\s*$")

# Preferred source for the canonical question list. Every run answers the same
# twenty; C3 is the portal default, so it is the natural reference.
_REFERENCE_ORDER = ("C3", "C0", "C5")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunAnswer:
    """One configuration's recorded answer to one question."""

    config: str
    question_id: str
    question: str
    answer: str
    sources: list[dict[str, str | None]]
    sources_recorded: bool
    omitted_chunks: int | None
    used_demo_sources: bool
    latency_ms: float | None
    retrieval_ms: float | None
    generation_ms: float | None
    iteration_count: int | None
    stop_reason: str | None
    verification: dict[str, Any] | None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "config": self.config,
            "question_id": self.question_id,
            "question": self.question,
            "answer": self.answer,
            "sources": self.sources,
            # Distinguishes "cited nothing" from "this run recorded no source
            # block". Without it an empty list would read as the former.
            "sources_recorded": self.sources_recorded,
            # How many retrieved passages were dropped to fit the context
            # budget — the clearest single number for what retrieval found
            # versus what generation was actually shown.
            "omitted_chunks": self.omitted_chunks,
            "used_demo_sources": self.used_demo_sources,
            "latency_ms": self.latency_ms,
            "retrieval_ms": self.retrieval_ms,
            "generation_ms": self.generation_ms,
            "iteration_count": self.iteration_count,
            "stop_reason": self.stop_reason,
            "verification": self.verification,
        }


def available_configs() -> list[str]:
    """Configuration directories that actually hold answers, in run order."""
    if not EVAL_ROOT.exists():
        return []
    configs = [
        directory.name
        for directory in EVAL_ROOT.iterdir()
        if directory.is_dir() and any(directory.glob("q*.txt"))
    ]
    return sorted(configs, key=_config_sort_key)


def _config_sort_key(name: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """C0 … C5 in order, with C1-CONTROL beside C1 rather than at the end."""
    match = re.match(r"^C(\d+)", name)
    return (int(match.group(1)) if match else 99, name)


@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def _summary(config: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    """`summary.csv` keyed by question id. Cached; a finished run never changes."""
    path = EVAL_ROOT / config / "summary.csv"
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    rows: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    try:
        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
            for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
                question_id = (row.get("id") or "").strip()
                if question_id:
                    rows[question_id] = row
    except OSError:
        return {}
    return rows


def _number(value: Any) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _split_answer(body: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, str | None]], int | None]:
    """Separate the answer from the source block and the trailing metadata line.

    Without this the answer rendered on the comparison page carried the
    harness's own formatting with it — a `Sources:` list and a
    `[C3 | model | retrieval …ms]` line — which is output for a terminal, not
    an answer the system gave.
    """
    heading = body.find(_SOURCES_HEADING)
    if heading == -1:
        # No source block: strip only the trailing metadata line.
        lines = [line for line in body.splitlines() if not _TRAILER_LINE.match(line.strip())]
        return "\n".join(lines).strip(), [], None

    answer = body[:heading].strip()
    sources: list[dict[str, str | None]] = []
    omitted: int | None = None

    for line in body[heading + len(_SOURCES_HEADING) :].splitlines():
        source_match = _SOURCE_LINE.match(line)
        if source_match:
            sources.append(
                {
                    "marker": f"[S{source_match.group(1)}]",
                    "label": source_match.group(2),
                    "url": None,
                }
            )
            continue

        url_match = _URL_LINE.match(line)
        if url_match and sources:
            # The URL belongs to the label immediately above it.
            sources[-1]["url"] = url_match.group(1)
            continue

        omitted_match = _OMITTED_LINE.match(line)
        if omitted_match:
            omitted = int(omitted_match.group(1))

    return answer, sources, omitted


def load_answer(config: str, question_id: str) -> RunAnswer | None:
    if not _QUESTION_FILE.match(question_id):
        return None

    path = EVAL_ROOT / config / f"{question_id}.txt"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None

    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return None

    # The log, where the run recorded one. Located by the first line beginning
    # an object at column zero, because the answer above can contain braces.
    log: dict[str, Any] = {}
    start = text.find("\n{")
    if start != -1:
        try:
            log = json.loads(text[start:])
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            start = -1

    body = text[:start] if start != -1 else text
    answer, sources, omitted = _split_answer(body)

    row = _summary(config).get(question_id, {})
    retrieval = log.get("retrieval") or {}

    wall = _number(row.get("wall_seconds"))
    return RunAnswer(
        config=config,
        question_id=question_id,
        question=str(row.get("question") or log.get("question") or ""),
        answer=answer,
        sources=sources,
        sources_recorded=_SOURCES_HEADING in body,
        omitted_chunks=omitted,
        used_demo_sources=bool(log.get("used_demo_sources")),
        latency_ms=_number(log.get("latency_ms")) or (wall * 1000 if wall else None),
        retrieval_ms=_number(log.get("retrieval_ms")) or _number(row.get("retrieval_ms")),
        generation_ms=_number(log.get("generation_ms")) or _number(row.get("generation_ms")),
        iteration_count=retrieval.get("iteration_count"),
        stop_reason=retrieval.get("stop_reason"),
        verification=log.get("verification") or None,
    )


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def questions() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Every evaluated question, from `summary.csv` — the one file every run has."""
    configs = available_configs()
    if not configs:
        return []

    reference = next((name for name in _REFERENCE_ORDER if name in configs), configs[0])
    rows = _summary(reference)
    return [
        {
            "id": question_id,
            "question": (row.get("question") or "").strip(),
            "category": (row.get("category") or "").strip(),
        }
        for question_id, row in sorted(rows.items())
        if (row.get("question") or "").strip()
    ]


__all__ = [
    "EVAL_ROOT",
    "RunAnswer",
    "available_configs",
    "load_answer",
    "questions",
]

"""The API's single point of contact with the knowledge service.

Two problems this module exists to solve, both consequences of measured
behaviour rather than of taste.

**Building a pipeline is expensive and must happen once.** It loads the
embedding model and, for C3 and later, the cross-encoder. Constructing one per
request would add seconds to every question and multiply memory on a machine
that is already tight. So pipelines are cached per configuration and built on
first use.

**Answering blocks for minutes.** `Pipeline.ask()` is synchronous and takes
between 60 and 330 seconds depending on configuration. Calling it from an async
route would stall the event loop and freeze every other request in the process.
So the generator runs in a worker thread and its events cross into async code
through a queue.

The set of configurations the portal will serve is deliberately narrow. C3 is
the default because the evaluation showed C4's extra ~95 seconds changes the
retrieved evidence on 2 questions in 20; C5 is offered explicitly, for a user
who asks for the answer to be checked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import queue
import threading
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

import anyio
from app.core.logging import get_logger

logger = get_logger(__name__)

# What a client may ask for, and what each means in plain language. Anything
# else is refused: the portal is not a research console, and letting arbitrary
# configuration names through would let a user select a pipeline nobody has
# evaluated.
PORTAL_CONFIGS: dict[str, str] = {
    "C3": "Standard — hybrid retrieval with cross-encoder reranking",
    "C5": "Verified — adds iterative retrieval and answer verification",
}
DEFAULT_CONFIG = "C3"

_pipelines: dict[str, Any] = {}
_lock = threading.Lock()

_SENTINEL = object()


def resolve_config(name: str | None) -> str:
    """Validate a requested configuration, or fall back to the default."""
    if not name:
        return DEFAULT_CONFIG
    key = name.strip().upper()
    if key not in PORTAL_CONFIGS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown configuration {name!r}. Available: {', '.join(sorted(PORTAL_CONFIGS))}"
        )
    return key


def get_pipeline(config_name: str) -> Any:
    """Return the cached pipeline for a configuration, building it if needed.

    Double-checked under a lock: two simultaneous first requests would
    otherwise each load an embedding model, which on this hardware is a
    multi-second, multi-hundred-megabyte mistake.
    """
    pipeline = _pipelines.get(config_name)
    if pipeline is not None:
        return pipeline

    with _lock:
        pipeline = _pipelines.get(config_name)
        if pipeline is None:
            from rag.config import get_config
            from rag.factory import build_pipeline

            logger.info("building_pipeline", config=config_name)
            pipeline = build_pipeline(get_config(config_name))
            _pipelines[config_name] = pipeline
    return pipeline


async def answer_stream(question: str, config_name: str) -> AsyncIterator[Any]:
    """Yield `rag.streaming.Event`s from a worker thread, without blocking.

    The pipeline is synchronous and slow. Rather than wrap each stage in an
    async shim — which would mean a second implementation of the answering path
    and the drift that comes with it — the whole generator runs on a thread and
    pushes events into a queue this coroutine drains.

    The queue is bounded. If a client stops reading, the producer blocks on a
    full queue rather than accumulating an unbounded answer in memory.
    """
    from rag.streaming import answer_events

    pipeline = get_pipeline(config_name)
    events: queue.Queue[Any] = queue.Queue(maxsize=64)

    def produce() -> None:
        try:
            for event in answer_events(pipeline, question):
                events.put(event)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported to the client below
            logger.exception("answer_failed", config=config_name)
            events.put(exc)
        finally:
            events.put(_SENTINEL)

    thread = threading.Thread(target=produce, name="rag-answer", daemon=True)
    thread.start()

    while True:
        item = await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(events.get)
        if item is _SENTINEL:
            break
        if isinstance(item, Exception):
            raise item
        yield item


__all__ = [
    "DEFAULT_CONFIG",
    "PORTAL_CONFIGS",
    "answer_stream",
    "get_pipeline",
    "resolve_config",
]

"""Phase 6b: authentication and the admin gate.

Split deliberately. `TestTokens` and `TestPasswords` need neither a database nor
FastAPI, because the rules they cover — what expires, what is refused, what a
wrong password does — are the ones worth pinning precisely. The route tests
override the database dependency with a stub rather than standing up
PostgreSQL, so the whole file runs in CI without services.

Two behaviours here would be silent if broken, and both get their own test: a
refresh token accepted as an access token, and a placeholder signing key
accepted in production.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import jwt
import pytest
from app.core.config import settings
from app.models.enums import UserRole
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.api import deps
from app.core.security import (
    INSECURE_DEFAULT_KEY,
    INSECURE_EXAMPLE_KEY,
    InsecureConfigurationError,
    create_token,
    decode_token,
    hash_password,
    insecure_key_reason,
    verify_password,
)
from app.main import app


class _FakeUser:
    """Enough of `User` for the dependency chain."""

    def __init__(self, role: UserRole = UserRole.ADMIN, active: bool = True) -> None:
        self.id = uuid.uuid4()
        self.email = "admin@pce.local"
        self.full_name = "Administrator"
        self.role = role
        self.is_active = active
        self.password_hash = hash_password("correct-horse")
        self.last_login_at = None


class _FakeSession:
    """A stand-in for the SQLAlchemy session, returning one known user."""

    def __init__(self, user: _FakeUser | None) -> None:
        self.user = user

    def get(self, _model, ident):  # noqa: ANN001
        if self.user is None or str(self.user.id) != str(ident):
            return None
        return self.user

    def scalar(self, _statement):  # noqa: ANN001
        return self.user

    def commit(self) -> None:
        pass

    def close(self) -> None:
        pass


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _no_leaked_overrides() -> Iterator[None]:
    """Clear dependency overrides after every test in this file.

    Autouse rather than tied to the `client` fixture, because several tests
    install a *second* database stub mid-test. If cleanup depended on
    requesting `client`, forgetting it would leave a stubbed database in place
    for whatever ran next — a failure that appears in an unrelated test.
    """
    yield
    app.dependency_overrides.clear()


def _client_for(user: _FakeUser | None) -> TestClient:
    """A client whose database contains exactly this user, or nobody."""
    app.dependency_overrides[deps.get_db] = lambda: _FakeSession(user)
    return TestClient(app)


@pytest.fixture
def user() -> _FakeUser:
    return _FakeUser()


@pytest.fixture
def client(user: _FakeUser) -> TestClient:
    return _client_for(user)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestPasswords:
    def test_a_hash_verifies_its_own_password(self) -> None:
        digest = hash_password("correct-horse")
        assert digest != "correct-horse"
        assert verify_password("correct-horse", digest)

    def test_a_wrong_password_does_not_verify(self) -> None:
        assert not verify_password("wrong", hash_password("correct-horse"))

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("password", "digest"),
        [("", "x"), ("pw", ""), ("pw", "not-a-bcrypt-hash")],
    )
    def test_malformed_input_is_false_not_an_exception(self, password: str, digest: str) -> None:
        """A corrupt hash should fail the login, not the request. Raising here
        would turn one bad row into a 500 that distinguishes it from a wrong
        password."""
        assert verify_password(password, digest) is False

    def test_the_same_password_hashes_differently_each_time(self) -> None:
        """bcrypt salts. Equal digests would mean the salt was lost."""
        assert hash_password("same") != hash_password("same")


class TestTokens:
    def test_a_token_round_trips_with_its_claims(self, user: _FakeUser) -> None:
        claims = decode_token(create_token(user.id, "admin"))
        assert claims["sub"] == str(user.id)
        assert claims["role"] == "admin"
        assert claims["type"] == "access"
        assert claims["jti"]

    def test_a_refresh_token_is_not_an_access_token(self, user: _FakeUser) -> None:
        """The check that stops a stolen refresh token granting days of API
        access instead of one exchange at the refresh endpoint."""
        refresh = create_token(user.id, "admin", "refresh")
        with pytest.raises(jwt.InvalidTokenError):
            decode_token(refresh, expected_type="access")
        assert decode_token(refresh, expected_type="refresh")["type"] == "refresh"

    def test_an_expired_token_is_rejected(self, user: _FakeUser) -> None:
        expired = create_token(user.id, "admin", "access", expires_delta=timedelta(seconds=-1))
        with pytest.raises(jwt.ExpiredSignatureError):
            decode_token(expired)

    def test_a_token_signed_with_another_key_is_rejected(
        self, user: _FakeUser, monkeypatch
    ) -> None:
        token = create_token(user.id, "admin")
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "secret_key", "a-different-key-entirely")

class TestThePlaceholderKeyIsRefusedInProduction:
    """The silent total bypass this guard exists to prevent.

    There are two published placeholders, not one: `config.py` declares a
    default, and `.env.example` overrides it with a different string. Copying
    `.env.example` to `.env` — the documented first step — therefore produces a
    key the field default never sees. A guard that knew only the field default
    would let exactly the realistic case through while appearing to cover it.
    """

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("key", [INSECURE_DEFAULT_KEY, INSECURE_EXAMPLE_KEY])
    def test_production_refuses_to_sign_with_a_published_key(self, key: str, monkeypatch) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "secret_key", key)
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "app_env", "production")
        with pytest.raises(InsecureConfigurationError):
            create_token(uuid.uuid4(), "admin")

    def test_the_key_env_example_actually_ships_is_one_of_them(self) -> None:
        """Read the file rather than trusting the constant.

        This fails if someone edits `.env.example` and leaves the guard behind
        — the drift that made the guard useless in the first place.

        It skips in the container, and that is not a detail to gloss over: the
        image is built with `context: ./backend`, so `.env.example`, which
        lives at the repository root, is not there and never will be. Under
        `docker compose exec api pytest` this assertion does not run. The same
        check therefore also exists as `scripts/check_secret_key.py`, which
        runs on the host where the file is visible and needs no dependencies.
        Run that; this copy only earns its keep on a host-side pytest.
        """
        example = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".env.example"
        if not example.exists():
            pytest.skip(
                "no .env.example in this tree (expected in the container) — "
                "run scripts/check_secret_key.py on the host instead"
            )
        shipped = [
            line.split("=", 1)[1].split("#")[0].strip()
            for line in example.read_text().splitlines()
            if line.startswith("SECRET_KEY=")
        ]
        assert shipped, "SECRET_KEY vanished from .env.example"
        for key in shipped:
            assert insecure_key_reason(key) is not None, (
                f"{key!r} ships in .env.example but the guard would accept it"
            )

    def test_a_short_key_is_refused_in_production(self, monkeypatch) -> None:
        """A key someone typed by hand is not a key."""
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "secret_key", "hunter2")
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "app_env", "production")
        with pytest.raises(InsecureConfigurationError):
            create_token(uuid.uuid4(), "admin")

    def test_development_with_the_default_key_warns_but_works(self, monkeypatch) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "secret_key", INSECURE_DEFAULT_KEY)
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "app_env", "development")
        assert create_token(uuid.uuid4(), "admin")

    def test_production_with_a_real_key_is_fine(self, monkeypatch) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "secret_key", _REAL_KEY)
        monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "app_env", "production")
        assert create_token(uuid.uuid4(), "admin")

"""Phase 6: the chat endpoint's wire format and its guardrails.

No database, no Ollama, no Chroma. The RAG service is replaced with a fake
event stream, because what is under test here is the transport: does an event
reach a browser in a form it can parse, and are the two things that must not
leak — an unevaluated configuration, and a silently truncated stream — actually
prevented.

`rag/tests/test_streaming.py` covers what the events *contain*.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.api.routes import chat
from app.main import app
from app.services import rag_service


class _Event:
    def __init__(self, name: str, data: dict) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.data = data


def _fake_stream(events: list[_Event]):
    async def stream(question: str, config_name: str) -> AsyncIterator[_Event]:
        for event in events:
            yield event

    return stream


def _parse_sse(body: str) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    """Parse the response the way a browser's EventSource would."""
    out: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
    for block in body.split("\n\n"):
        if not block.strip():
            continue
        name = data = None
        for line in block.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("event: "):
                name = line[len("event: ") :]
            elif line.startswith("data: "):
                data = json.loads(line[len("data: ") :])
        assert name is not None, f"event block without a type: {block!r}"
        out.append((name, data))
    return out


@pytest.fixture
def client() -> TestClient:
    return TestClient(app)


class TestTheWireFormat:
    def test_events_parse_as_a_browser_would_parse_them(
        self, client: TestClient, monkeypatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            chat,
            "answer_stream",
            _fake_stream(
                [
                    _Event("stage", {"stage": "retrieval", "status": "started"}),
                    _Event("token", {"text": "The intake "}),
                    _Event("token", {"text": "is 180."}),
                    _Event("answer", {"answer": "The intake is 180."}),
                    _Event("done", {"latency_ms": 1.0}),
                ]
            ),
        )
        response = client.post("/api/v1/chat", json={"question": "intake?"})

        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.headers["content-type"].startswith("text/event-stream")
        # Without this, a proxy buffers the whole answer and the streaming is
        # invisible to the user — the failure looks like a hang, not a bug.
        assert response.headers["x-accel-buffering"] == "no"

        events = _parse_sse(response.text)
        assert [name for name, _ in events] == ["stage", "token", "token", "answer", "done"]
        assert events[-2][1]["answer"] == "The intake is 180."

    def test_a_newline_in_the_payload_cannot_split_an_event(
        self, client: TestClient, monkeypatch
    ) -> None:
        """SSE is newline-delimited, so an unescaped newline in an answer
        would truncate the event and hand the client half a JSON document."""
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            chat,
            "answer_stream",
            _fake_stream(
                [
                    _Event("answer", {"answer": "Line one.\nLine two.\n\nLine three."}),
                ]
            ),
        )
        response = client.post("/api/v1/chat", json={"question": "multi line?"})

        events = _parse_sse(response.text)
        assert len(events) == 1
        assert events[0][1]["answer"] == "Line one.\nLine two.\n\nLine three."

    def test_a_mid_stream_failure_becomes_an_error_event(
        self, client: TestClient, monkeypatch
    ) -> None:
        """The status line has already gone out, so a 500 is impossible.

        A truncated stream is indistinguishable from a completed one, so the
        only honest option left is to say so in-band.
        """

        async def exploding(question: str, config_name: str):
            yield _Event("stage", {"stage": "retrieval", "status": "started"})

"""Schema tests.

The unit tests here need no database. The integration tests need a live
PostgreSQL and are what CI runs; they are the safety net for a schema whose
migration was generated rather than hand-written.

The drift check is the important one. It applies every migration to an empty
database and then asks Alembic to diff the result against `Base.metadata`. Any
difference — a column the migration missed, a type that does not match, an
index declared on the model but never created — fails the build. Without it,
a model change merged without its migration would only surface when a query
hit a column that does not exist in production.
"""

import pytest

from app.models import enums

        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)

        for table in Base.metadata.tables.values():
            for column in table.columns:
                name = getattr(column.type, "name", None)

class TestMigrationsNeverCreateEnumTypes:
    """No migration may create an enum type as a side effect of CREATE TABLE.

    Enum types are owned by revision 0002_enum_types. Two reasons this must be
    enforced rather than remembered:

    1. Six of the fourteen types are shared between tables — `run_status` by
       both `eval_runs` and `ingestion_jobs`. A CREATE TABLE that owns its type
       fails on the second table with DuplicateObject, even on a database where
       nothing had created it before.
    2. Alembic's autogenerate does NOT carry `create_type=False` across from
       the model. It re-renders a type from its name and values alone, so every
       regenerated migration reintroduces the fault unless `render_item` in
       alembic/env.py rewrites it.

    This exact defect broke `alembic upgrade head` on a completely fresh
    database. The test needs no database, so it fails in seconds rather than
    after a container build.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def _migration_sources() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        from pathlib import Path

        versions = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "alembic" / "versions"
        return [(p.name, p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in sorted(versions.glob("*.py"))]

    def test_no_migration_uses_bare_sa_enum(self) -> None:
        offenders = [name for name, src in self._migration_sources() if "sa.Enum(" in src]
        assert offenders == [], (
            f"{offenders} use sa.Enum(), which creates the type during CREATE TABLE. "
            "Use postgresql.ENUM(..., create_type=False); alembic/env.py's render_item "
            "hook does this automatically for newly generated migrations."
        )

    def test_every_enum_column_disables_type_creation(self) -> None:
        import re

        offenders: list[str] = []
        for name, src in self._migration_sources():
            for match in re.finditer(r"postgresql\.ENUM\((?:[^()]*)\)", src):
                if "create_type=False" not in match.group(0):
                    offenders.append(f"{name}: {match.group(0)[:70]}...")
        assert offenders == [], f"enum columns that would create their type: {offenders}"

    def test_the_env_hook_that_keeps_this_true_is_present(self) -> None:
        """Without render_item, the next autogenerate silently undoes the fix."""
        from pathlib import Path

        env = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "alembic" / "env.py").read_text()
        assert "render_item" in env, (
            "alembic/env.py has lost its render_item hook. The next "
            "`alembic revision --autogenerate` will emit sa.Enum(...) again and "
            "`alembic upgrade head` will fail on a fresh database."
        )
        assert "create_type=False" in env


@pytest.mark.integration
@pytest.mark.skipif(not os.environ.get("POSTGRES_HOST"), reason="needs a live PostgreSQL")
class TestMigrationsAgainstADatabase:
    """The safety net for a migration that was generated rather than reviewed
    line by line."""

    def test_migrations_leave_no_drift_against_the_models(self) -> None:
        """Apply every migration, then diff the result against Base.metadata.

        An empty diff means the migration and the models agree. A non-empty one
        names exactly what is missing.
        """
        from alembic.autogenerate import compare_metadata
        from alembic.migration import MigrationContext

        from app.db.session import engine

        with engine.connect() as connection:
            context = MigrationContext.configure(
                connection,
                opts={"compare_type": True, "compare_server_default": True},
            )
            diff = compare_metadata(context, Base.metadata)

        # Alembic reports enum types it did not create as removals; they are
        # created by hand in 0002, so ignore that one category.
        meaningful = [entry for entry in diff if "remove_type" not in str(entry[0])]
        assert meaningful == [], f"schema drift between migrations and models: {meaningful}"

    def test_every_table_exists(self) -> None:
        from sqlalchemy import inspect

        from app.db.session import engine

        actual = set(inspect(engine).get_table_names())
